item.title: Six-Lens Poem Reading and the Story Behind It
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
Skills have flooded the workplace. This is the first one I am publishing.

It Started with Nonsense

A friend sent me this image, calling it an authentic Wu Daozi. I looked and looked and could not spot the forgery. It must be real.

I replied at once:

Nothing wrong here. He was a man of that age. He saw it with his own eyes. Du Mu came later - what is he fantasizing about? Gates opening one after another? Did those gates even need to open? Just because Wu Daozi has some random Cantonese accent, why should posterity refuse him? The tragedy of history.

Joke aside, once that poem came up - Passing the Huaqing Palace, the first of three quatrains - I thought again of this year’s trip to Xi’an. I had given a full day to the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor, and never made it to the neighboring Lishan Garden or Huaqing Palace, the very stage of this poem.

长安回望绣成堆， 山顶千门次第开。 一骑红尘妃子笑， 无人知是荔枝来。

Picture the scenes line by line, from far to near, from urgency to ease: it has the feel of a camera moving through a film. A classic that still reaches us today has its reasons.

So I had AI dig up sources and background from every angle. The back-and-forth ran long. I asked a lot of questions and kept pushing for fact-checks. Near and far, open and hidden, piece by piece the material locked onto my mental map of Chang’an and the Tang. It was rich.

But if every poem that sparks my curiosity means another half-day of Q&A, will that kill the urge to explore? That is when I decided to find out whether there is a fuller, more standard way to read a poem - and to build one for myself.

Minkowski and the Literary Light Cone

Set poetic artistry aside for a moment. As a carrier of information, a poem should at least have time, place, and person. From the broad age down to the moment of writing, time has a thread. Geography too runs from large to small, converging on the space and scene the poem holds, enriching its background and even its subject. The human factor needs no argument: the author’s life path often dominates what the poem does.

What rose in my mind then was a Minkowski spacetime diagram. A great work is, at bottom, a spacetime event. That stretches the concept a bit, but the author’s time and space - and all the information they bring - really do meet at the origin.

I call this metaphor the literary light cone. Before a great work is born, it is already like this. Information inside the cone helps shape the work; information outside never reaches the author. That is why every work is unique, stamped with a person and a spacetime.

AI reminded me I was too fixed on the physical world and ignoring the conceptual one. The cone needs another factor: literary tradition - what shaped the author’s thought and style, how that uniqueness compares with contemporaries, and what it did to later literature.

Literature itself becomes a bridge between past and future. In a future the author never reaches, there is not only influence on later writing, but also later readings of this work. Readings shift with the temper of an age and what society needs. That is how the work’s life continues. As long as someone is still reading it, it is immortal.

Finally, pull back from past and future. Set all outside influence aside and look only at the work itself. A literary reading of the text alone can stand apart from the rest. It is the origin of the whole literary light cone.

To read a poem is to start from that origin and follow the threads - convergence in the past, divergence into the future.

How the Six-Lens Poem Reading Skill Was Born

From that picture, a method seemed to surface: dig back through era, geography, biography, and literary tradition; look forward to later literary influence and later readings; and, in place, unfold the poem’s own literary qualities.

Once the idea was clear, building the Skill was easier than expected. I polished it back and forth, testing poems of every kind - Tang and Song, lyric and discursive, famous and obscure, even anonymous Han yuefu. Plenty of problems showed up. I kept pushing AI to reason from first principles and revise the Skill’s rules. On a few ultra-niche pieces it still misfires, but in most cases it beats simply saying “help me interpret XXX.”

Here is how the Skill works:

  1. Gather widely from six angles - Era (世), Place (地), Person (人), Craft (文), Tradition (统), Reception (受) - dig layer by layer, and sort each angle on its own.
  2. Fold the four past-cone factors - Era, Place, Person, Tradition - into a timeline table that ends at the origin.
  3. Run an obsessive, exhaustive fact-check: fix errors, add detail.
  4. Output in the required format the two main parts - Six-Lens Reading and Convergence Timeline - plus a little supporting material.

The hardest problem was still hallucination. When sources run dry, AI invents facts, and can even warp a poem’s emotional color. Most of the work on this Skill went into fighting that. Step 3 became an extremely strict anti-hallucination gate.

A note on how I build Skills. If a task is not open-ended, has a clear deliverable, and that deliverable’s quality can be judged in plain language, you should refine the Skill in a loop:

  1. Start with a one-off task. Point out problems as it works so it learns your preferences and goals. Then have it write the first version of the Skill for itself.
  2. Run the task with that Skill. More problems will show. Keep pointing them out and iterating the Skill.
  3. After a few rounds, ask whether it can now draft a rubric for judging quality. It usually can. Have it produce one, save it as a document, and use it for verification.
  4. Iteration speeds up. Spin up a sub-agent that knows only the Skill. The main agent scores the sub-agent’s work against the rubric it wrote, flags issues, and confirms them with you one by one. You will find Skill bugs and rubric bugs; keep iterating both.
  5. After one such pass, ask whether this can be a repeating loop. It usually says yes. Have it write the loop rules down and follow them.
  6. Then each round needs only two things from you: judge the issues it found, and order the next round.

I have built more complex Skills this way - seven or eight code files, a dozen-plus docs. The Skill contents are a black box to me; I never read them. I only watch inputs and outputs. Still, I stably get what I want. When a loop cannot fix something, you step in, learn enough of the logic, and nudge it toward likely failure modes.

Frontier models today have no glaring capability gaps. What they lack is your preferences and goals - the stuff in your head, not in the training data. In building this kind of loop, once it really knows those, it has a strong shot at doing the job well. Even the anti-hallucination mechanisms in the Skill were mostly invented by AI under my insistence and refusals.

Honestly, of the six angles - Era, Place, Person, Craft, Tradition, Reception - the last three were ones AI pushed me to add. Together they make this Six-Lens Poem Reading method.

Using the Six-Lens Poem Reading Skill

Download the Skill here:

https://skills.victor42.work/poem-six-lens/

Three sample readings:

  • Six-Lens Poem Reading: 乐游原
  • Six-Lens Poem Reading: 使至塞上
  • Six-Lens Poem Reading: 清平乐·村居

One caution: treat the timeline like the light cone. It only strings events in time. You cannot claim direct cause between them, but you can sense the subtle stacking of many factors that finally sparks. Like leaving work one day and suddenly wanting a detour for teppanyaki - if there is a reason, it probably was not born that day.

The Skill has flaws too. With so many angle shifts, AI reading those complex links easily falls into its own jargon haze. But if you truly care about the poem and stay with it, you will respect the information density.

One more warning: the Skill triggers a burst of web searches in a short window. In a cloud sandbox it often gets blocked. Prefer a local agent.

That is enough AI talk. I built this Skill to enjoy classical poetry - to serve real life. Even a die-hard STEM geek like me can feel the beauty in these poems; a thousand years of transmission is not an accident. If a poem truly interests you, Six-Lens Poem Reading should only be a starting point. The distant spacetime behind it is something you can explore with AI.

item.title: 六合读诗与幕后故事
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
Skill在职场已经泛滥成灾了，我才首次公开我的Skill。

从一段胡说八道开始

朋友发来这么一张图：说是吴道子的真迹，我左看右看也没看出哪里造假了，应该是真的。

我一看，回复道：

没毛病，他就是那个年代的人，他亲眼见到的。杜牧个后世人，YY个什么劲，还次第开，那门用得着开吗？就因为吴道子有点不知道哪来的广东口音，后世人凭什么不认。历史的悲哀。

玩笑归玩笑，既然提到了这首《过华清宫绝句三首·其一》，我又回味起了今年的那次西安旅行。当时安排了一整天给秦始皇陵，隔壁的丽山园和华清宫就没来得及去，这首诗的主场正是那里。

长安回望绣成堆， 山顶千门次第开。 一骑红尘妃子笑， 无人知是荔枝来。

认真想象这首诗的画面，一句句细品，由远及近，由急到缓，有种电影镜头版的质感。千古名篇能传到今天，自有不凡之处。

于是让AI从各个角度查询资料、了解背景。讨论过程来回拉锯了很久，我问了大量问题，反复让AI做事实核查。远的近的，明的暗的，种种信息逐渐对接上我对长安和唐朝的认知框架，收获满满。

但如果将来再满足我对另一首诗的好奇心，还要这样来回问答小半天，会不会打击我探索的积极性？至此，我下决心搞清楚，解读一首诗有没有比较全面和标准方法，我得给自己来一套。

闵可夫斯基和文学光锥

诗词的艺术性暂且放一边，它作为一种信息传递的载体，时间、地点、人物三要素总该有吧。从宏大的时代背景，到写作那一刻，时间层面一定有它的脉络。地理的因素也是由大到小，逐渐汇聚到诗中所载的空间和现场，丰富了诗的背景甚至主体。人的因素更不必说了，作者的人生轨迹在诗中的作用显而易见，往往占主导地位。

想到这里，我脑子里的画面竟然是闵可夫斯基时空图，伟大的作品本质是一个时空事件。虽然有点偷换概念，但作者所处的时间、空间，它们带来的全部信息确实在原点位置交汇。

我把这个比喻称为文学光锥，伟大的作品在诞生的那一刻前就是如此。光锥内的信息帮助塑造了作品，而光锥外的信息影响不到作者，这使得任何作品都有独特性，带有他个人和所处时空的独特印记。

在AI的提醒下，我意识到我过于关注物理世界，忽略了概念世界。光锥里还需要补一个因素：文学传统，作者的文学思想和风格受到了哪些影响，与同时代的作者相比产生了哪些独特性，又对后世的文学有什么样的影响。

就这样，文学本身成为了一座桥梁，连接了过去和未来。在作者到不了的未来，不仅有他对后世文学的影响，也有后世人对他这份作品的解读。解读也是会变化的，会根据时代风貌和社会需要解读出不同的含义，这是这份作品生命的延续。只要还有人在解读它，它就是不朽的。

最后，从过去和未来逐渐收回来，抛开所有外部影响，只看这份作品本身。对它本身文学性的解读可以独立于其他因素之外，是整个文学光锥的原点。

我们读诗，就是要从原点出发，顺藤摸瓜看清过去的收敛与未来的发散。

六合读诗Skill的诞生

顺着这个画面，解读一首诗的方法似乎浮出水面了：从时代、地理、生平、文学传统向前追溯深挖所有相关信息，也向后调查它对后世文学的影响和后人的解读，同时原地展开这首诗本身的文学性特质。

想法有了，Skill的诞生比想象中容易。来回打磨，用各种题材的诗词去测试它，唐代的宋代的，抒情的说理的，知名的小众的，甚至连作者佚名的汉乐府诗也试过了。暴露出不少问题，反复让AI从第一性原理思考解法，调整Skill的规则。可能遇到一些极小众的诗词时，还会发挥失常，但绝大多数情况下，比直接跟AI说“帮我解读XXX”质量高多了。

这个Skill的工作方式是这样的：

  1. 从 世（时代）、地（地理）、人（生平）、文（文学性）、统（文化传统）、受（后人解读） 六个角度广泛收集信息，逐层深挖，每个角度分别梳理。
  2. 把 世、地、人、统 四个过去光锥的因素整理成时间线，列成表格，表格终点指向原点。
  3. 进行丧心病狂的穷尽式事实核查，纠正错误，补充更多细节。
  4. 按要求的格式输出 六合解读 和 收敛时间线 两大主要部分，以及少量补充信息。

这其中遇到过的最大的问题还是幻觉，AI容易在一些查不到具体资料时编造事实，甚至把一首诗的情感色彩都说歪了。制作这个Skill，最多的精力花在了和幻觉斗争上，最终把第3步逼成了一道极其严苛的防幻觉核查关卡。

这里分享一点我做Skill的心得。如果一个任务不是开放性的，有明确的产出物，而且产出物的品质有衡量标准，这标准用自然语言能说得清楚。你就应该通过循环来打磨这个Skill：

  1. 一开始是给AI个一次性任务，指出它完成过程中的各种问题，它会了解你的偏好和目标。这时候就可以指挥它自己给自己写第一版Skill。
  2. 然后再让它用这Skill来执行任务，一般还会有各种问题，继续指出来，让它迭代Skill。
  3. 反复几次后，你问它，你现在能不能自己制定出一套评判标准，来评判任务完成质量。它大概率会说可以，那就让它产一套，把标准沉淀成文档存好，用来验证。
  4. 接下来打磨速度就可以大大加快了。让它开子代理来执行任务，子代理是什么都不知道的，它只知道这个Skill的内容。主代理拿着它自己写的标准来衡量子代理的工作，让它判断有哪些问题，和你逐一确认。确认过程中既会发现Skill的问题，也可能发现评判标准的问题，让它继续迭代。
  5. 这样一轮下来，再跟它说，这是不是可以构成一个循环，反复迭代？它大概率也会说可以。你就让它把循环的规则也沉淀为文档，照着执行。
  6. 最后，每一轮迭代就只需要做两件事：评价它发现的问题，以及命令新开一轮迭代。

我做过一些比较复杂的skill，里面7、8个代码文件，十几个文档，就是用这种方式循环出来的。Skill的内容对我来说完全是个黑盒，我一眼都没看过，我只关注输入和输出。但无论如何，最后稳定得到了我要的结果。当然，如果有它反复循环都解决不了的问题，就需要你向前一步，了解相关的执行逻辑，提示它可能的问题方向。

前沿的AI模型到今天，能力已经没有明显的短板了。它缺的只是你的偏好和目标，这是装在你脑子里的东西，它的训练数据里没有。在打造这种迭代循环的过程中，只要它充分了解你的偏好和目标，就大有希望把事情做好。甚至Skill里那些防幻觉的机制，大多是在我的坚持和否定下，AI自己想出来的。

老实说，世、地、人、文、统、受这6个角度，后3个都是AI提醒我补上的。共同构成了这套“六合读诗”。

使用六合读诗Skill

Skill可以在此下载：

https://skills.victor42.work/poem-six-lens/

它的3首解读示例：

  • 六合读诗：乐游原
  • 六合读诗：使至塞上
  • 六合读诗：清平乐·村居

需要注意的是，看待时间线，也要像看待光锥一样，它仅仅是把事件在时间上串起来了。你不能说它们相互间一定有直接因果关系，但你能意会那种多重因素微妙叠加、累积而成的迸发。就像你有一天下班，就莫名想绕路去吃一家铁板烧，如果真有原因，大概率也不在当天。

当然，这个Skill缺点也不是没有。由于角度多重变换，AI在解读这其中复杂联系时，很容易陷入它的某种自嗨中，导致黑话连篇。但如果对这首诗真的感兴趣，耐着性子看下去，那信息密度你是会认可的。

还有一点要提醒的是，这个Skill会短时间触发大量网络搜索，在云端沙盒里用，容易被拦。推荐在本地Agent里用。

AI的东西到此为止，做这个Skill还是为了欣赏古诗词，是为现实生活服务的。古诗词中的美，连我这种Geek到死的理科生都能感受到，流传千年自有它的道理。真的对一首诗词感兴趣，六合读诗应该只是一个起点，背后的遥远时空，你可以带着AI一起探索。

item.title: I Ditched My Living Room Coffee Table and Sectional Sofa
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
Redesigning our living room with AI to create a beautiful and functional space for the family

Sudden Inspiration and Determination

It all started when I was chatting with a friend from my former company about reading. She told me she had specifically remodeled her living room for that purpose. Looking at the pictures of her home, I was deeply inspired. It made me think about what kind of living room a modern small family living in the city actually needs. The answer becomes clear once you think it through. However, busy adults rarely have the courage to make changes to make their lives just a little bit better.

But determination is something that comes out of nowhere, without needing any psychological preparation. As soon as I finished the chat, I re-evaluated everything from scratch and started the living room redesign project that very day.

It has been nearly ten years since our home renovation was completed. Back then, I put a lot of effort into it, even taking a few months off between jobs to focus on it: A Designer’s Renovation Notes

At that time, we didn’t have a child, nor did we think about whether we would have one. The initial living room design was for two adults, featuring a standard layout with a sofa, a coffee table, and a TV stand. That living room accompanied my wife and me through many weekends eating snacks and watching movies.

Since our daughter was born, the function of the living room has drifted far from its original purpose. The TV stand and coffee table turned into toy tables. Half of the sofa was piled with plush toys, and the other half was filled with clothes brought in from the balcony that we were too lazy to fold. When adults wanted to sit down, we ended up on the dining chairs in the dining room, rarely in the living room. Although the sofa was comfortable, getting to it was difficult, and finding a place to sit was even harder. The entire living room became a space for our daughter’s solo play and family reading, but her toys still frequently spilled over into the hallway, blocking the way.

Essentially, the center of attention in the living room had shifted from a single TV to multiple scattered activities. Even for a childless city family, the core of the living room is no longer the TV. With no guests visiting and no cable TV, contemporary young city dwellers spend their living room hours on phones, tablets, books, or the elliptical and yoga mat. Of course, the TV still holds some ground as a console gaming screen, but it is no longer essential.

From this perspective, the huge sectional sofa and coffee table actually severely lowered space utilization. Facilities should serve life, allowing the living room to adapt to its actual functions and better support them: playing, reading, and family time. It also formally establishes a shared space for family activities - something my daughter will need later, and I have plenty of books I want to read here too.

What Kind of Living Room Do We Actually Need?

To answer this question, we must start from first principles, following a logical thinking sequence:

  1. Analyze the current state of living room functions and add the extra functions we want.
  2. Map these functions to physical items to ensure every need is met.
  3. Inventory the required items to check if they all fit; if it is too crowded, make trade-offs.
  4. Once items are selected, plan the spatial layout.
  5. Sourcing and actual remodeling.

For the first three steps, a simple table is enough. The current functions of our living room include:

Function Current State
Kids’ play TV stand, ❌Coffee table, ❌Sofa
Family reading ❌Sofa
Projector projection Small side table
Adults resting -
Book storage Column bookshelf
Toy storage TV stand, ❌Coffee table
Sundries storage TV stand, Small side table, ❌Coffee table
Balcony laundry staging ❌Sofa
Workout Elliptical trainer
Sleeping ❌Sofa
Relaxing -

We want to keep the existing functions as much as possible, especially restoring the adults resting function. We can also introduce a new function: relaxing, and if space permits, add a massage chair.

Identify the functions that need to be significantly enhanced, then add or replace items with higher space utilization to fill the functional gaps:

Function Current State New Item
Kids’ play TV stand, ❌Coffee table, ❌Sofa Low bookshelf set
Family reading ⏫ ❌Sofa Sofa bed, Armchair
Projector projection Small side table -
Adults resting ⏫ - Sofa bed, Armchair
Book storage ⏫ Column bookshelf Low bookshelf set
Toy storage ⏫ TV stand, ❌Coffee table Low bookshelf set
Sundries storage TV stand, Small side table, ❌Coffee table -
Balcony laundry staging ❌Sofa Armchair
Workout Elliptical trainer -
Sleeping ❌Sofa Sofa bed
Relaxing - Massage chair

The key here is the low bookshelf set, placed in a row against the wall. The bookshelf countertop can replace the coffee table as a toy station, and the inside greatly increases the living room’s storage capacity. The sofa bed is another great addition: it can seat one adult and one child for reading picture books, and it can unfold for guests to stay a few nights. The open space freed up by removing the sectional sofa can also be used for playing, making the living room feel much larger and preventing toys from invading the hallway.

After reviewing the layout, we realized a standalone massage chair might not fit as it would take up too much play space for our daughter. However, we can consider a massage cushion in the future.

By this point, the items to be purchased were basically finalized. There was no need to change the hard decoration; modifying the soft furnishings was enough to achieve our goals.

AI Becomes the Designer Mocking Up Layouts

Now we enter the fourth step: planning the spatial layout.

During the renovation years ago, I did this step very thoroughly. I taught myself SketchUp on the fly and started drawing 3D diagrams. I wasn’t trying to render photo-realistic sales-office-level mockups; I just wanted to accurately reflect the dimensions of all items in a model, down to the centimeter level, to judge whether they would fit and how they could be arranged for the most convenient use.

Although the learning curve was steep, this approach was incredibly effective - it was our source of truth for the interior layout. For this small living room redesign project, I wanted to use a similar method. However, I had forgotten most of my SketchUp skills, and since I am not a professional interior designer, there was no need to relearn the software. In the era of AI, creating a 3D model of simple geometric shapes is just a matter of speaking.

We could reuse most of the dimensions from the old renovation measurements, and we quickly measured the few missing numbers to fill the gaps. Then, I sent the spatial constraints and basic dimensions to the AI. The output was mostly correct on the very first try. After two or three rounds of minor adjustments, the empty living room model was created:

This is a trapezoidal area with a south wall of 339 cm, a north wall of 281 cm, and an east balcony glass door of 333 cm. The two eastern corners are right angles, and the west side is open, leading to the dining room. Considering the presence of the curtains on the east, the actual usable area might be reduced by about 20 cm in width on the east side.

The space has the following constraints:

  • There are power outlets and an Ethernet port in the middle of the north wall, so the router must be placed here.
  • Other power outlets are located at the northeast, southeast, and southwest corners of the space.
  • The south wall has large-area wallpaper, making it unsuitable for direct projection. For projection, we must use the north wall or add a screen on the south wall.
  • The passage leading to the balcony across the living room runs parallel to the north wall, about 40 cm away, and must be at least 80 cm wide and kept clear.

I asked the AI to divide the space into three layers: the base layout, the current state, and the planned state. These three layers could be toggled on and off independently, making it easy to compare the effects before and after the redesign.

Then, I started directing it like a client directing a designer, telling it to put the sofa here, the elliptical there, make the coffee table longer, and the column bookshelf thinner… As a former UI designer who was once told by product managers and operations to make buttons redder or move cards two pixels closer, I felt a slight twinge of nostalgia.

In any case, after two evenings of back-and-forth, the AI completed the task beautifully. For this kind of work, you need an AI with strong visual capabilities. Even if you don’t use it to look at images, a model with strong visual understanding has a clear advantage in grasping spatial orientation. Antigravity 2.0 indeed worked precisely as directed.

The completed 3D diagram. This is the current state, where there is almost nowhere to stand in the living room except for the passage.

The planned layout. The elliptical trainer was moved near the glass door, removing a major visual and movement obstacle between the dining room and the living room. A row of low bookshelves against the wall became the main base for my daughter’s toys. The small side table was pushed out slightly by the bookshelves, so we turned it to run north-south to avoid blocking the passage. Since we rarely use the projector, there was no need for the sofa bed and armchair to face the northern TV wall; placing them opposite each other is better for conversation. These items surround an open play area, leaving plenty of room for large building blocks, puzzles, and other activities.

Two top-down views make it easier to see how much space has been freed up.

This was actually enough to give me a clear idea of what the result would look like. But to help my wife and daughter visualize the outcome, I had Codex read the project to understand all the dimension details. Then, I took a photo of the current room and fed it to Codex, using its image generation capability to directly generate a mockup of the redesigned room.

This is the general idea, though it altered some details of the items. Also, the image generation model probably hadn’t seen two sofas facing each other in the middle of a living room very often, so it still rendered a conventional layout.

But that was fine. The dimensions were quite accurate, and it looked close enough to a “movie day” setup. We hadn’t selected the furniture yet; to generate a truly precise mockup, we would need to feed it the product images of the chosen furniture. Since the three of us already had a clear picture in our minds, there was no need to obsess over this step.

Purchasing and Completion

There isn’t much to say about purchasing - spending money is the best part, and we bought everything in a single day.

Once all the items arrived, we got it all done in one day. In the morning, we hired someone to haul away the old sofa and coffee table. In the afternoon, my wife cleaned the room while I assembled the cabinets and sofa, and the new living room took shape.

My daughter said she had so much fun redesigning the living room. She even helped install two handles on the row of bookshelves against the wall.

The brown armchair in the bottom right of the photo felt out of place. The backrest wasn’t high enough, making it uncomfortable to sit on, so we returned it. The new one is on its way.

Just a day later, my daughter quickly filled the space with her toys. To prevent her from bumping into the sharp corners of the metal bookshelves, we laid a table mat on top that extends about 1 cm outward.

Compared to before, the room indeed feels much more spacious. Several days later, my wife was still talking about how satisfied she was with this living room redesign.

Bringing a little change to our lives can bring a lot of sunshine. As for AI, who says it can only be used for work and making money?

item.title: 我扔掉了客厅茶几与组合沙发
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
和AI共同完成了一场客厅小改造，女儿和老婆赞口不绝。

突如其来的灵感和决心

起因是和前司的朋友聊天，聊到读书，朋友说她为此专门改造了客厅。我看完她家照片大受启发，现代人小家庭城市生活，到底需要什么样的客厅，在脑袋里一推演就会有答案。只是忙碌的成年人，很少能拿出勇气做点改变，让自己的生活变得更美好一点点。

不过，决心这个东西，说来就来的，不需要什么心理准备。我聊完立马从头推演了一遍，当天就开启客厅的改造计划。

我家已经装修完快10年了，费了许多心思，甚至换工作间隙花了几个月时间专门来搞这事：一个设计师的装修笔记

当时没小孩，也没想过会不会有。客厅初始设计服务两个成年人，沙发茶几电视柜，标准布局。这样的客厅，陪伴我和老婆度过了不少啃着鸡爪鸭脖看电影的周末。

自有女儿以来，客厅的作用早已偏离初衷。茶几电视柜变成玩具桌，沙发一半堆玩偶，一半堆阳台收进来又懒得叠的衣服。大人歇脚都在餐厅餐椅，很少在客厅。因为沙发虽舒服，但走进去很困难，找到地方坐下更困难。整个客厅成了小孩独自娱乐和家庭阅读的空间，但女儿玩具还是经常摆到过道上来，挡住去路。

本质是，客厅这个空间的注意力重心，从单一的电视，变成了多处分散的形式。即使没有小孩，城市小家庭的客厅，核心也早已不是电视了。没有客人，不看电视台节目，当代城市年轻人的客厅时光，要么给了手机平板，要么给了书，要么给了椭圆机瑜伽垫。当然，电视作为游戏机屏幕仍有一定地位，但不是必须。

这么看，硕大的组合沙发和茶几反而严重拉低了空间利用率。设施应为生活服务，让客厅顺应它的实际功能，并更好地承担这些功能：玩耍、阅读与亲子时光。同时也正式开辟一个家庭共同活动的空间，女儿之后会需要的，我自己也有不少书想在这读。

到底需要什么样的客厅

要回答这个问题，得从第一性原理出发，有个一定不会出错的思考顺序：

  1. 梳理客厅的功能现状，并加入我们想要的额外功能。
  2. 把这些功能对应到物品上，让每个需求都被满足。
  3. 盘点所需物品，是不是都放得下，过于拥挤就要取舍。
  4. 选定物品后，安排空间摆放。
  5. 采购与实际改造。

前3步简单做个表就行了，客厅当前功能包括：

功能 现状
小孩玩耍 电视柜、❌茶几、❌沙发
家庭阅读 ❌沙发
投影仪播放 小边桌
大人歇脚 -
书籍收纳 柱状书柜
玩具收纳 电视柜、❌茶几
杂物收纳 电视柜、小边桌、❌茶几
阳台衣物暂存 ❌沙发
运动 椭圆机
睡觉 ❌沙发
放松 -

现有功能尽量保留，大人歇脚的功能我们希望恢复。另外还可以考虑引入新功能：放松，如果空间允许，加入按摩椅。

标出哪些功能需要特别增强。然后添置或换上空间利用率更高的物品，补上功能缺口：

功能 现状 新物品
小孩玩耍 电视柜、❌茶几、❌沙发 矮书柜组
家庭阅读⏫ ❌沙发 沙发床、单人沙发
投影仪播放 小边桌 -
大人歇脚⏫ - 沙发床、单人沙发
书籍收纳⏫ 柱状书柜 矮书柜组
玩具收纳⏫ 电视柜、❌茶几 矮书柜组
杂物收纳 电视柜、小边桌、❌茶几 -
阳台衣物暂存 ❌沙发 单人沙发
运动 椭圆机 -
睡觉 ❌沙发 沙发床
放松 - 按摩椅

这里面关键的是矮书柜组，靠墙放一整排。书柜台面可以代替茶几作为玩具基地，内部大大提升客厅收纳能力。沙发床是另一个好东西，平时可坐下一大一小，读个绘本没问题，客人来了也能展开住几晚。组合沙发让出的地面也能摆玩具，客厅的可用空间会大许多，玩具不容易再侵占过道了。

盘点过后，发现独立的按摩椅可能是放不下，会吞掉女儿太多玩耍空间，但以后可以考虑买按摩靠垫。

到这里，要添置的物品已经基本敲定。硬装不太有必要动，只改软装就能达到目的。

AI成了乙方改图狗

现在进入第四步，规划空间摆放。

当年装修时，我把这一步做得非常细，非常重。我临时自学的SketchUp，然后就开始咔咔上手画立体图。我不是为了渲染出那种难辨真假的售楼处级效果图，我只想把所有物品的尺寸精确反映在一个模型里，尺寸精确到厘米级，判断摆不摆得下，怎么摆用起来最顺手。

虽然学习成本高，这套真的很管用，是室内布置的关键真相源。在这小小的客厅改造项目里，我也想用这种方式。只是SketchUp的操作我真是忘差不多了，我也不是职业室内设计师，没必要再重温这玩意。现在AI时代，这种简单几何形的立体建模，真的动动嘴就行。

当年装修留下的尺寸测量记录，很多都能继续用，缺的少量数据临时量一下补上。然后，我把空间约束和基础尺寸信息，整理下发给AI，一轮输出就基本正确。再两三轮细节修正，空客厅就建模出来了：

这是一个南墙339cm、北墙281cm、东边阳台玻璃门333cm的梯形区域，东边两个角是直角，西边开放，通往餐厅。考虑东边窗帘的存在，实际可用面积可能还要减掉东边20cm宽。

空间内有如下制约条件：

  • 北墙中央有电源插座、网线口，所以路由器只能放在这里。
  • 其余的电源插座在空间的东北、东南、西南3个角。
  • 南墙有大面积墙纸，不适合直接投影。如果要投影，只能在北墙上，或者南墙加幕布。
  • 穿过客厅、通往阳台的通道，平行于北墙，距离北墙约40cm，宽至少需要80cm，不可被阻挡。

我让AI把空间分成了3层：底图、现状、计划，3层可以分别开关，方便我对比改造前后效果。

然后，我就开始像指挥乙方一样，告诉它沙发摆这里，椭圆机摆那里，茶几你画长点，圆柱书柜你画细点……作为一个曾经也被产品经理和运营指着屏幕让把按钮改红色、把卡片靠近2个像素的UI设计师，甚至有点心酸。

但是，不管怎样，经过了2晚的拉锯，AI漂亮地完成了任务。干这种活，就得用视觉能力强的AI，哪怕不用它看图，视觉能力强的模型对方位的理解也有明显优势。Antigravity 2.0，用起来确实指哪打哪。

完成后的立体图。这是现状，客厅除了那条通道，几乎无处下脚。

计划中的布局。椭圆机被放到了玻璃门边，餐厅和客厅间的一大视线障碍和动线障碍被移走。靠墙一排矮书柜，女儿玩具的主要基地。小边桌被书柜往外挤了些，所以改成南北向摆放，不挡通道。由于很少看投影仪，沙发床和单人沙发没必要对着北边电视墙，相对摆放更利于交谈。这些东西合围出一块开阔的游玩区，大型积木、拼图什么的都有地方玩了。

两张顶视图，更容易看出空间的明显释放。

其实到这里就可以了，改完什么样我心里有数。但为了让老婆和女儿能大概想象改造后的结果，我又让Codex读了这个项目，了解所有尺寸细节。再拍一张现状照片给它，用它的生图能力直接生成改造后的效果图。

大概是这么个意思，就是它把一些东西的细节样子给改掉了。另外，生图模型可能在训练时没怎么见过两个沙发在客厅中央隔空相对摆放，还是给我画成了常规摆法。

但问题不大，尺寸画得挺准确，就当是movie day的状态。家具还没有挑选，真要生成严谨的效果图，那应该在挑完家具后，把家具商品图也给它。既然一家三口脑子里都有画面了，这步就不必较真。

采购与完成

采购就没什么好说的了，花钱是最开心的，一天就买齐了。

东西全部收到后，一天搞定。上午请人搬走旧沙发茶几，下午老婆打扫屋子，我组装柜子和沙发，新客厅就成型了。

女儿说，今天改造客厅真开心。靠墙那排书柜，有2个把手还是女儿帮忙装的。

画面右下的棕色单人沙发，感觉很不协调，靠背也不够高，坐着不舒服，就给退了。新的还在路上。

才过一天，女儿就迅速用她的玩具把这块空间填满了。为了防止女儿在金属书柜边角撞伤，上面还铺了一层桌垫，向外突出来1cm左右。

相比之前，确实松快多了。好几天后老婆都还在念叨，说这次客厅改造得真满意。

给生活一点点变化，生活也会给我们很多阳光。至于AI，谁说只能用来工作和赚钱呢？

item.title: What is an AI Native Data System
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
How my data management evolved alongside tools

I am a power user of Excel and Google Sheets, relying on them heavily to manage both work and life.

Later, I migrated some of my heavier data management tasks to visual databases like Feishu Bitable. While they might look like Excel, they are fundamentally different beasts. With much stricter data rules than spreadsheets, they trade some flexibility for the raw power of a true database. You can easily link multiple tables and build highly complex data systems - more than capable of running a small business.

I once built a full-cycle task management system in Bitable, tracking everything from assignment to delivery. It seamlessly spun out weekly reports, project calendars, and annual stats. People asked for this system at least three times: a colleague for personal use, a manager for their team, and my previous employer for a company-wide rollout.

But no matter how powerful the tool, you still have to do the heavy lifting yourself.

I believe in what I call the “dishwasher philosophy”. The older generation often scoffs at dishwashers, arguing, “You still have to rinse the plates first. I could have just washed them by hand in that time!” Here is my take: washing by hand takes 15 minutes of pure human labor. Rinsing takes 5 minutes, and the machine runs for 40 - but that is still only 5 minutes of my time. I just bought back 10 minutes of my life.

To me, technology is a tool to reclaim my life.

Bitable has built-in AI features, and you can also use local Agents to control it via CLI or API. But if you try it, it feels like Usain Bolt running underwater - completely constrained. Bitable is not an AI-native product; it is designed for human eyes and human logic. Current AI Agents are text-based creatures, interacting with the world through code. Therefore, the most AI-native data system is simply a database.

I spent a day overhauling this system with AI. I stripped it back to the basics and took it entirely local. It no longer relies on cloud services or third-party apps. Now, it is just a lightweight local SQLite database, entirely read, written, and managed by AI. It automatically generates four pages based on the data: a calendar, recent tasks, historical tasks, and project stats. These serve as my dashboard and command center. Here is how it looks:

Need to squeeze in a last-minute request? I just tell the AI to push all tasks from today onwards back by one workday, and it even splits overnight tasks to skip the weekend. Just one sentence.

Finished a task? The AI automatically scans the schedule for the task’s last appearance, sets that as the delivery date, and marks it done. If I forget to add deliverable links or thumbnails, it nudges me to provide them. Again, just one sentence.

Want to add public holidays to the calendar? It is a non-standard request, but since you are using AI, it always finds a way to make it happen.

I am not saying this replaces Excel or Bitable entirely. Their perks are undeniable: WYSIWYG interfaces, cross-platform access, and zero environment dependencies. I still manage plenty of data in Google Sheets.

Watching the AI carefully but slowly read specs, write SQL, verify data, and update pages does not bother me one bit. Sure, I could have done it in seconds in Excel or Bitable. But over a full day of intensive use, who knows how many of those seconds the AI has bought back for me.

This system is open-source, so feel free to grab it. It will keep your work perfectly organized without draining your time on administrative chores: https://github.com/greenzorro/project-manager

item.title: 什么是AI原生的数据系统？
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
我的数据管理方式，随工具发展的几次变迁。

我Excel/Google Sheets用得很溜，大量用它们管理工作和生活。

后来，我曾经把一部分较重的数据管理任务迁移到飞书多维表这样的产品里。这类东西长得很像Excel，但本质上是完全不同的东西，是可视化数据库。它们比Excel有着严格得多的数据规范，限制灵活性的同时，释放了数据库天然带来的强大能力。可以更轻松建立多表关联，构建出结构非常复杂的数据系统，支撑一个小生意都不在话下。

我用多维表构建过任务管理系统，每一项工作任务从接收到交付，完整生命周期全都在里面。从中再派生出周报、排期日历、年度数据报表等用途。这套系统至少3次被别人要了去，一次是同事个人，一次是主管拿去管理团队，还一次是被前司拿去全员推行。

但再强大，毕竟免不了亲自动手。

我信奉一个“洗碗机哲学”：老一辈瞧不上这玩意，总觉得你不还是得先冲洗下再放进去吗，有这时间我早就手洗完了。我的道理是，手洗15分钟，投入人工15分钟；人工冲洗5分钟+洗碗机洗40分钟，人工只投入5分钟，我给自己的人生赢回了10分钟。

科技，在我这，是用来赎回生活的。

多维表本身也带AI功能，或者也可以用本地的Agent通过CLI或API来操作多维表。但你试过就知道，那过程就像博尔特在海底跑步，束手束脚的。多维表并不是一种AI Native的产品，它的形态是围绕人类视觉和理解而设计的。目前的AI Agent都是文字生物，代码是他们和世界交互的方式，最AI Native的数据系统就是数据库。

花了1天时间完成了这套系统的AI化改造。返璞归真，彻底本地化。它现在不用再依赖任何云端产品或第三方应用了，一个轻量级本地SQLite数据库，完全由AI来读写和管理。根据其中数据自动产生日历、近期任务、历史任务、项目统计4个页面，作为我观察数据的窗口，和发号施令的依据。效果如下：

插个临时需求？让AI把今天及以后的所有任务都延后一个工作日，跨天任务还能自动拆成两段避开周末。就一句话的事情。

有个任务完成了？AI自动去排期表里找，这个任务最后一次出现在哪一天，把那天作为交付日期，更新完成状态。如果缺了交付物链接、缩略图等信息，还主动提醒我补充。也是一句话的事情。

往日历里添加法定节假日，这种非标准用法，反正你用的是AI，它总有办法满足你。

不是说这种方法值得代替一切Excel或多维表，它们的优点也非常明显：所见即所得、跨平台、无环境依赖，我仍有许多数据是在Google sheets里管理的。

看着AI仔细但缓慢地读规范、写SQL、验证数据、更新页面，我一点也不嫌弃。如果是在Excel或多维表里，我可能十几秒就处理完了。但一天密集用下来，不知道AI又给我的人生赢回了多少个十几秒。

这套系统已经开源，欢迎取用。让你工作井井有条，又不用花太多时间在事务性任务上：

https://github.com/greenzorro/project-manager

item.title: A Travel Guide to Xinjiang Natural Scenery and Ethnic Culture
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
A conceptual framework for your first visit to Xinjiang.

Fresh from a trip to Xishuangbanna, I could not wait to research my next adventure: Xinjiang.

The furthest west I had previously been was an earlier trip to Dunhuang. I had zero baseline concept of traveling in Xinjiang, knowing only that the Tianshan Mountains divide the north from the south. I had only vague impressions of what distinct regions offered or what one could actually experience.

Xinjiang is immense. To filter destinations effectively, I spent two evenings working with AI - collecting, structuring, debating, and validating data - to synthesize this travel cognitive guide. It evaluates the travel experience across all fourteen prefecture-level administrative divisions from the twin lenses of natural scenery and ethnic culture. Combining this with meticulous study of administrative and topographic maps helped me build a clear mental model of Xinjiang tourism.

This is merely a starting point. A framework developed this way is inevitably high-level and may contain minor oversights. The fine details will ultimately be verified and refined by my own eyes and footsteps on the ground.

Part 1: Natural Scenery

Organized across 14 prefecture-level administrative divisions, surveying representative natural landscapes in each region

Overview: The Geographic Logic of Xinjiang

Xinjiang’s geography can be summarized in one classic phrase: Three Mountains Enclosing Two Basins.

  • Altay Mountains - Northern grasslands, taiga forests, and alpine lakes
  • Junggar Basin - Northern Gobi, gravel deserts, and oasis belts
  • Tianshan Mountains - Meadow steppes, snow-capped peaks, and river canyons (the natural divide between North and South)
  • Tarim Basin - Sand dunes, gravel wastes, river oases, and desert poplars (Populus euphratica)
  • Kunlun Mountains + Pamir Plateau - Ultra-high massifs, glaciers, and alpine plateau lakes

Northern Xinjiang Landscape Keywords: Grasslands, lakes, alpine forests, snow peaks - humid, lush, and scenic.

Southern Xinjiang Landscape Keywords: Sand deserts, Gobi wastes, sandstone canyons, desert poplars - vast, desolate, and rugged.

Eastern Xinjiang Landscape Keywords: Flaming Mountains, Yardang landforms, extreme basin heat - extreme and singular.

Northern Xinjiang (7 Prefectures & Cities)

1. Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture (Direct Admin Area) - The Jiangnan Beyond the Great Wall

The Ili River Valley forms a funnel-shaped opening facing westward into the Tianshan range, catching moist Atlantic air currents. It receives the highest rainfall and supports the densest vegetation in Xinjiang, celebrated as the “Wet Island of Central Asia.”

Landscape Summary: Alpine meadows + Schrenk spruce forests + glacial trekking trails + alpine lakes. This is the densest and most visually rich natural landscape corridor in Xinjiang.

Nestled along the southern slopes of the Altay Mountains at the northernmost tip of Xinjiang. The forest, lake, and snow mountain ecosystem centered around Kanas Lake reaches its aesthetic peak in autumn.

Natural Scenery Travel Planning Recommendations

What to Prioritize in Northern Xinjiang

  • Top Choice: Ili Valley (5-7 days): Grasslands + forests + lakes + glaciers. Highest scenic density in Xinjiang.
  • Pair with Altay (3-4 days): Kanas + Hemu village autumn colors (optimal seasons differ: Ili peaks June-August; Altay peaks September-October).
  • En-Route Stops: Sayram Lake (Bortala), Tianchi (Changji), Ghost City (Karamay).

What to Prioritize in Southern Xinjiang

  • Pamir Plateau (2-3 days ex-Kashgar): Muztagh Ata + Baisha Lake + Karakul Lake - epic high-altitude alpine terrain.
  • Canyon Route (Aksu): Tianshan Mysterious Grand Canyon + Wensu Grand Canyon - geological wonders.
  • Desert & Poplar Forests (Bayingolin / Hotan): Taklamakan Desert + Luntai Tarim Poplar Forest (peak in late October).

What to Prioritize in Eastern Xinjiang

  • Turpan (1-2 days): Flaming Mountains + Grape Valley + Karez Wells - oasis culture and extreme thermal topography.
  • Hami Dahaidao (1 day): Deep Yardang wilderness, optimal for off-road and expedition photography.

Part 2: Ethnic Culture

Structured based on data from the 2020 Seventh National Population Census

1. Provincial Demographic Composition Overview

The Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region has a resident population of 25.85 million, forming a diverse multi-ethnic society:

Ethnic Group Population Share of Total Population Share of Minority Population
Uyghur 11.62 million 44.96% 77.85%
Han 10.92 million 42.24% -
Other Minorities (Kazakh, Hui, Mongol, Kyrgyz, Xibe, etc.) 3.31 million 12.80% 22.15%

Core Insight: Uyghurs constitute the largest single ethnic group in Xinjiang, but do not exceed half of the total population. Han and Uyghur populations exist in an approximate 1:1 ratio, alongside 12.80% comprising over a dozen other minority groups distributed across autonomous prefectures. One cannot assume absolute Uyghur demographic majority simply from the administrative name of the autonomous region.

3. Spatial Patterns: The Complete Picture

3.1 Overall Geographic Distribution

Northern Xinjiang

  • Urumqi, Karamay, Changji, Bortala, Tacheng - Han majority populations with modern urban infrastructure
  • Ili River Valley - Vibrant multi-ethnic mosaic (Kazakh, Han, Uyghur, Hui, Xibe, Mongol)
  • Altay - Kazakh majority population (the only division where a non-Han group exceeds 50% in the north)

Eastern Xinjiang

  • Hami - Han ~71%, diverse ethnic communities
  • Turpan - Uyghur majority population

Southern Xinjiang

  • Bayingolin (Korla) - Han ~59%, a distinct demographic outlier in the south
  • Aksu - Uyghur majority population, Han ~26%
  • Kizilsu - Predominantly Uyghur and Kyrgyz populations (Han ~11%)
  • Kashgar - Uyghur ~97%, the cultural heartland of Southern Xinjiang
  • Hotan - Uyghur ~93%, the densest concentration of Uyghur population

3.2 Minority Settlement Zones

Primary Uyghur Settlement Areas: Kashgar, Hotan, Aksu, Turpan, Kizilsu

Primary Kazakh Settlement Areas: Altay, Tacheng, Ili

Multi-Ethnic Mosaic Zones (No single minority exceeding 50%): Urumqi, Karamay, Changji (Hui vs Kazakh parity), Bortala (Mongol, Uyghur, Kazakh tripartite balance)

The historical naming of these autonomous prefectures reflects mid-20th century geopolitical considerations and minority settlement policies, presenting interesting contrasts with contemporary demographic shifts.

5. Two Primary Minority Cultural Traditions

Why Focus Primarily on These Two Groups?

While Xinjiang hosts dozens of recognized ethnic groups, Uyghur and Kazakh cultures offer the most prominent cultural touchstones and mature travel infrastructure:

  • Mongol: Population in Xinjiang is relatively small with dispersed cultural tourism resources.
  • Hui: Widely distributed throughout towns without forming a single concentrated scenic cluster.
  • Kyrgyz, Tajik, Xibe: Modest population bases with specialized frontier tourism facilities still evolving.

Uyghur and Kazakh cultures provide clear regional identities paired with well-established visitor facilities.

5.1 Uyghur Culture - Oasis Agrarian Civilization

Cultural Profile

Dimension Content
Linguistic Family Turkic language family (shared roots with Kazakh and Turkish)
Religious Tradition Sunni Islam
Demographics 11.62 million across Xinjiang (44.96% of total regional population)
Core Heartland South of Tianshan Mountains, oases encircling the Tarim Basin
Economic Baseline Settled oasis agriculture + vibrant Bazaar market commerce

Key Cultural Experiences

  • Bazaar Culture: Kashgar Grand Bazaar, Hotan Jade Bazaar - Central Asia’s most expansive traditional market systems, condensing commerce, language, handicrafts, and culinary traditions.
  • Old Town Architecture: Gaotai Ancient Homes in Kashgar Old City, labyrinthine earthen alleys representing pristine traditional Islamic vernacular architecture.
  • Historic Mosques: Id Kah Mosque in Kashgar (among China’s largest historical mosques), Jiaman Mosque in Hotan.
  • Oasis Orchard Life: Grape trellises, fig groves, and pomegranate orchards defining traditional courtyard life.
  • Cuisine: Polo (lamb pilaf), baked samsa, tandoor roasted lamb, laghman hand-pulled noodles, gangzi jar mutton, yogurt zongzi.
  • Craftsmanship: Traditional glazed pottery, Atlas silk weaving, Hotan jade carving, Yengisar knives, and classical Muqam musical suites.
  • Festivals: Eid al-Adha (Corban Festival) and Eid al-Fitr (Rozi Festival) - checking festival calendars reveals peak communal celebrations at bazaars and mosques.

Optimal Travel Destinations

Region Experience Highlights
Kashgar Prefecture Bazaars + Old City alleys + historic mosques: the intact cultural core of traditional Uyghur heritage
Hotan Prefecture Jade bazaars, traditional silk workshops, authentic rural oasis life
Aksu Prefecture Transition zone between Uyghur heartland and northern trading routes, less commercialized
Turpan City Quintessential oasis farming (Grape Valley, Karez wells), closest proximity to Urumqi

Top Recommendation: Kashgar. Kashgar is the undisputed cultural capital of Southern Xinjiang and the most vibrantly preserved living Silk Road metropolis in China.

5.2 Kazakh Culture - Steppe Nomadic Civilization

Cultural Profile

Dimension Content
Linguistic Family Turkic language family (cognate with Uyghur with distinct phonetic systems)
Religious Tradition Sunni Islam (with pronounced secular and nomadic cultural synthesis)
Demographics Approximately 1.56 million in Xinjiang (~10% of regional minority population)
Core Heartland Western Northern Xinjiang: from Ili River Valley north to the Altay range
Economic Baseline Seasonal transhumance pastoralism, migrating between summer alpine meadows and winter lowlands

Key Cultural Experiences

  • Steppe Pastures: Summer alpine meadows (Nalati, Kalajun, Tangbula) dotted with white felt yurts (kiez uy).
  • Seasonal Transhumance: Large-scale pastoral livestock migrations in spring and autumn - a vital cultural spectacle (typically May-June and September-October).
  • Yurt Hospitality: Visiting authentic Kazakh pastoral yurts, drinking salted milk tea, tasting baursak pastries, and listening to dombra folk ballads.
  • Equine Heritage: Horseback riding, sheep-dragging contests (kokpar), horse racing, and the “Girl Chase” courtship game (Kyz Kuu).
  • Musical Traditions: Dombra (two-stringed plucked lute), Aken improvisational poetry duels (designated UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage).
  • Cuisine: Boiled mutton platter (et), Naryn noodles with shredded meat, kumis (fermented mares milk), baursak fried dough, milk tea.
  • Felt Crafts: Traditional felt embroidery showcasing geometric patterns and vivid botanical motifs.

Optimal Travel Destinations

Region Experience Highlights
Ili Prefecture (Direct) Nalati, Kalajun, and Tangbula grasslands: most mature Kazakh pastoral tourism infrastructure
Altay Prefecture Highest Kazakh demographic density (52.8%), authentic pastoral life, alongside Tuvan hamlets in Hemu and Kanas
Tacheng Prefecture Baketu border port, remote mountain pastures, uncommercialized and quiet

Top Recommendation: Ili. While Altay possesses higher Kazakh demographic density, the Ili River Valley combines dramatic mountain grassland landscapes with well-developed pastoral hospitality.

6. Contrast Between the Two Civilizations

Dimension Uyghur (Oasis Agrarian) Kazakh (Steppe Nomadic)
Geography South of Tianshan, Tarim Basin oases North of Tianshan, Ili Valley to Altay pastures
Mode of Production Sedentary farming + Bazaar commerce Seasonal transhumance, pastoral migration
Dwelling Style Earth-and-timber courtyard residences Portable white felt yurts (yurt)
Core Culinary Naan bread, polo pilaf, kebabs, fresh fruits Boiled mutton, naryn noodles, milk tea, kumis
Religious Practice Islamic traditions deeply woven into daily town life Islamic heritage synthesized with nomadic customs
Musical Forms Classical Twelve Muqam orchestral suites Dombra lute + Aken improvisational poetry
Social Center The Bazaar (public market) Steppe gatherings, seasonal festivals
Architectural Focus Mosques, minarets, shaded alleyways Alpine pastures, yurts, transhumance trails
Optimal Travel Season Year-round (avoiding mid-summer heat) Summer peak (June to September during green meadows)

Their primary commonality is their shared homeland within Xinjiang. Aside from that, their languages, pastoral versus oasis economies, culinary staples, music, architectural forms, and rhythms of life present captivating contrasts. Experiencing both dimensions provides a complete perspective on Xinjiang’s rich cultural tapestry.

3. Core Itinerary Recommendations

  1. If selecting only one region: First-time visitors should choose Northern Xinjiang (Ili). The visual drama of alpine meadows, sapphire lakes, spruce forests, and yurt pastures provides immediate impact with mature infrastructure.
  2. If time permits (10+ days): Direct flight to Kashgar (South: 3-4 days) → domestic flight to Urumqi → Ili Valley (North: 5-6 days), experiencing both oasis and nomadic civilizations in a single journey.
  3. Special autumn journey for Kanas: Fly directly to Altay to bypass Urumqi transfers, traveling straight to Hemu and Kanas for peak autumn foliage.
  4. Southern travel considerations: Hotan and Kashgar rural areas have lower Mandarin penetration; hiring local guides or using translation apps aids deeper engagement. Summer heat in Turpan is intense (approaching 50°C).

4. Commute Distance and Driving Duration Analysis

Xinjiang’s geographic vastness exceeds what travelers from densely populated eastern provinces typically anticipate. Transit time is a critical variable when planning compact itineraries.

item.title: 新疆自然风光与民族文化旅行指南
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
一份首次造访新疆前的旅行认知框架。

刚从西双版纳回来，就迫不及待开始研究下一场旅行了，目标新疆。

以前最远只去过敦煌，对新疆旅游完全没有概念，就只知道天山是南疆北疆分界。具体各个地方有什么，去了能体验到什么，只有很模糊的认识。

新疆非常大，为了筛选目的地，我花2个晚上和AI反复收集、梳理、讨论、验证，得出了这份旅行认知指南。从自然风光和民族文化两个角度，审视新疆各个地级行政单位的旅行体验。结合反复观察新疆行政区图和地形图，帮我建立了新疆旅游的初步概念，帮助非常大。

当然，这仅仅是个起点。这份指南的认知一定是片面的，颗粒度也很粗，可能也有些未发现的错误，细节就要靠自己的眼睛和双脚去补充和修正了。

第一部分：自然风光

按14个地级行政区划分，梳理各区域的代表性自然景观

总览：新疆自然风光的底层逻辑

新疆的景观可以用一句话概括：三山夹两盆。

  • 阿尔泰山 — 北疆草原·森林·湖泊
  • 准噶尔盆地 — 北疆戈壁·荒漠·绿洲
  • 天山 — 草原·雪峰·峡谷（南北疆分界线）
  • 塔里木盆地 — 沙漠·戈壁·绿洲·胡杨
  • 昆仑山 + 帕米尔高原 — 极高山·冰川·高原湖

北疆的景观关键词：草原、湖泊、森林、雪山——湿润、丰沛、秀美

南疆的景观关键词：沙漠、戈壁、峡谷、胡杨——苍茫、壮阔、粗犷

东疆的景观关键词：火焰山、雅丹、盆地极热——极端、独特

北疆（7个地州市）

1. 伊犁哈萨克自治州（州直）— 塞外江南

伊犁河谷是天山向西敞开的开口，接收来自大西洋的湿润气流，是整个新疆降水最多、植被最丰茂的区域。被称为"中亚湿岛"。

景观 亮点 特色标签
喀拉峻草原 “立体草原”，世界自然遗产，从谷底到山巅层次分明 世界遗产·立体草原
库尔德宁 世界自然遗产，天山雪岭云杉林最完整的保留地 世界遗产·雪岭云杉
那拉提草原 中国六大最美草原之一，空中草原景观 国家5A·空中草原
唐布拉草原 “百里长卷、天然画廊”，沿S315省道一路花海 百里画廊·公路景观
赛里木湖 新疆海拔最高、面积最大的高山冷水湖，大西洋最后一滴眼泪（行政属博州但紧邻伊犁） 高山湖泊·蓝
果子沟大桥 穿越天山的壮观高架桥，连接赛里木湖与伊犁河谷 工程景观
昭苏草原 天马之乡，油菜花海（7月），夏塔古道通向天山冰川 天马文化·冰川古道
夏塔古道 翻越天山南北的古驿道，通往木扎尔特冰川，徒步圣地 冰川徒步·古道
恰西森林公园 原始云杉林，伊犁河谷的秘境，游客远少于那拉提 原始森林·小众

景观类型总结：高山草原 + 雪岭云杉林 + 冰川古道 + 高山湖泊。是新疆自然风光最集中、最丰富的区域。

2. 阿勒泰地区 — 东方瑞士

阿尔泰山南麓，新疆最北端。以喀纳斯湖为中心的森林-湖泊-雪山景观在秋季达到巅峰。

景观 亮点 特色标签
喀纳斯湖 深邃的高山湖泊，变色湖水（随季节呈蓝、绿、白），“湖怪"传说 5A·摄影师天堂
禾木村 图瓦人村落，原始木屋+白桦林+晨雾，中国最美古村落之一 图瓦村落·秋色
白哈巴 西北第一村，位于边境线上，哈萨克族与图瓦人混居 边境村落·原始
可可托海 额尔齐斯河源头的花岗岩神钟山，地质公园 世界地质公园
五彩滩 额尔齐斯河畔的雅丹地貌，北岸彩石南岸森林，日落绝美 雅丹·日落
乌伦古湖 新疆第二大淡水湖，海滨浴场，冬季冰捕 湖泊·渔猎

景观类型总结：高山湖泊 + 原始森林（白桦/泰加林） + 雅丹地貌 + 边境村落。秋季（9月中-10月初）是最佳季节。

3. 博尔塔拉蒙古自治州 — 赛里木湖的门户

景观 亮点 特色标签
赛里木湖 新疆海拔最高（2071m）、面积最大的高山冷水湖，湖水深蓝通透，环湖公路 高山湖泊·5A
哈日图热格 原始森林峡谷，博尔塔拉河源头 森林峡谷·小众

博州面积小，核心就是赛里木湖。但它恰好卡在从乌鲁木齐进入伊犁的门户位置，几乎所有人都会经过。

4. 塔城地区 — 草原与边境

景观 亮点 特色标签
甘家湖梭梭林 世界最大的原始梭梭林自然保护区 荒漠林·生态
鹿角湾 巴尔鲁克山的牧场，夏季高山草甸 高山牧场
巴克图口岸 中国与哈萨克斯坦的边境口岸，可远眺哈方 边境口岸

塔城地区的自然风光相对分散，旅游开发程度在北疆中最低，适合小众深度游。

5. 昌吉回族自治州 — 天山北坡入口

景观 亮点 特色标签
天山天池 新疆最标志性的景点，天山博格达峰下的高山湖泊 5A·标志性景点
江布拉克 高山草原+麦田+针叶林，连绵的万亩麦海（7-8月金黄） 高山草甸·麦海
S101国防公路 天山北坡的丹霞地貌+草原+峡谷，被称为"天山地理画廊” 自驾公路·丹霞

昌吉紧邻乌鲁木齐，天池是新疆的"名片级"景点，半日即可往返。S101是近年新火的公路自驾线路。

6. 乌鲁木齐市 — 城市与天山门户

景观 亮点 特色标签
南山风景区 天山北坡的牧场和森林，乌鲁木齐最近的山地景观（1.5h车程） 近郊牧场
博格达峰 天山东段最高峰（5445m），天池即在其北坡 雪山（远观）

乌鲁木齐主要是交通枢纽，自然风光不算突出，南山是市民周末去处。

7. 克拉玛依市 — 雅丹与戈壁

景观 亮点 特色标签
乌尔禾魔鬼城（世界魔鬼城） 中国最美三大雅丹之一，风蚀城堡群，日落时分为最佳 雅丹地貌·5A
艾里克湖 克拉玛依唯一的天然淡水湖，戈壁中的绿洲 湖泊·小众

克拉玛依的自然景观以雅丹地貌为核心，魔鬼城是从乌鲁木齐去喀纳斯的必经之路上的经典停靠点。

南疆（5个地州）

8. 巴音郭楞蒙古自治州 — 新疆最大的地州

巴州面积47万平方公里，占全疆1/4，横跨天山南北。既有北疆的草原湖泊，又有南疆的沙漠戈壁。

景观 亮点 特色标签
巴音布鲁克草原 中国第二大草原，天山南麓最大高山牧场，天鹅湖湿地，九曲十八弯日落 高山草原·天鹅·日落
博斯腾湖 中国最大的内陆淡水湖，芦苇荡，沙漠边缘的大湖 大型淡水湖·芦苇
塔里木胡杨林（轮台） 世界面积最大的原始胡杨林，塔里木河畔，金色胡杨（10月底-11月初） 胡杨林·沙漠河畔
罗布人村寨 塔里木河畔的罗布人后裔村落，沙漠+湖泊+胡杨 沙漠绿洲·人文
天山石林 巴音布鲁克附近的高山石林，罕见地貌 高山石林·小众
库木塔格沙漠 与城市零距离接触的沙漠（若羌/且末方向），世界上距城市最近的沙漠 沙漠·徒步

景观类型总结：巴州的景观跨度极大——北有巴音布鲁克草原（天山中段），中有博斯腾湖（焉耆盆地），南有塔里木胡杨林（塔克拉玛干边缘）。是唯一一个同时拥有草原、大湖、沙漠三种极端景观的地州。

9. 阿克苏地区 — 天山南坡的峡谷王国

景观 亮点 特色标签
天山神秘大峡谷（克孜利亚） 天山支脉的红褐色巨型峡谷，库车附近，“中国的科罗拉多” 红色峡谷·5A
温宿大峡谷（托木尔大峡谷） 比克孜利亚更大更壮观，丹霞+雅丹+盐岩地貌叠加 大峡谷·丹霞
托木尔峰 天山最高峰（7443m），天山山脉的主峰 极高山·登山
塔里木河源头 中国最长的内陆河的源头区域 河流·源头
沙雅胡杨林 塔里木河中游的原始胡杨林，规模仅次于轮台 胡杨林

景观类型总结：以峡谷地貌为核心竞争力。克孜利亚和温宿大峡谷是南疆最震撼的地质景观。阿克苏还拥有天山最高峰托木尔峰，但常规旅行无法接近。

10. 克孜勒苏柯尔克孜自治州 — 帕米尔高原的门户

景观 亮点 特色标签
奥依塔克红山 火山地貌，红褐色山体与冰川交汇，形成"冰与火"的奇观 火山冰川·小众
木吉火山口 帕米尔之眼，1500年前形成的火山口群，四周被高原湿地和冰川包围 火山口·高原湿地
卡拉库里湖 慕士塔格峰下的高山冰蚀湖，海拔3600m 高原湖泊·倒影

克州面积小、人口少，自然景观集中在帕米尔高原入口。奥依塔克和木吉是摄影师的小众秘境。

11. 喀什地区 — 帕米尔高原与西域尽头

景观 亮点 特色标签
帕米尔高原 “世界屋脊”，平均海拔4000m+，中巴公路穿越的核心区域 高原·极致公路
慕士塔格峰 “冰山之父”，海拔7546m，终年积雪，帕米尔的地标 极高山·攀登圣地
白沙湖（恰克拉克湖） 帕米尔高原最美的湖泊，一半白沙一半碧水 高原湖泊·白沙
卡拉库里湖 慕士塔格峰脚下的冰蚀湖，经典倒影 高原湖泊
盘龙古道 昆仑山脉中的600多道弯盘山公路，航拍圣地 公路景观
布伦口沙湖 沙山与湖水交汇，帕米尔高原上的沙湖奇观 沙湖
塔什库尔干 帕米尔高原上的小城，石头城遗址，通往巴基斯坦的红其拉甫口岸 高原古城·边境

景观类型总结：帕米尔高原是喀什地区自然风光的核心——极高山、高原湖泊、冰川、极致公路。这是整个新疆海拔最高、景观最"极端"的区域。

12. 和田地区 — 塔克拉玛干的核心

景观 亮点 特色标签
塔克拉玛干沙漠 世界第二大流动沙漠，“进去出不来"的死亡之海 流动沙漠
沙漠公路 穿越塔克拉玛干的沙漠公路（和田→阿拉尔），最孤绝的公路体验 极端公路
尼雅遗址 “东方庞贝”，塔克拉玛干深处的精绝国遗址 古遗址·探险

和田地区的自然风光主要是沙漠。它是整个新疆最"干"的地方，景观以苍茫荒凉为特征。沙漠公路是南疆环线中极具仪式感的一段。

东疆（2个地级市）

13. 吐鲁番市 — 火焰与极热

景观 亮点 特色标签
火焰山 《西游记》原型，夏季地表温度可达80°C，赤红山体绵延百里 极端高温·地标
葡萄沟 火焰山中的绿洲峡谷，葡萄架遮天蔽日 绿洲峡谷·果园
库木塔格沙漠 世界上距城市最近的沙漠，从鄯善县城步行可达 城市沙漠
坎儿井 地下水利工程，与万里长城、京杭大运河并称中国古代三大工程 水利工程
吐峪沟 最古老的维吾尔族村落，峡谷中有千佛洞 峡谷村落·文化

吐鲁番是中国海拔最低（-154m）、夏季最热的地方。自然景观围绕"极热+绿洲+沙漠"展开。

14. 哈密市 — 东天山与戈壁

景观 亮点 特色标签
大海道 新疆最壮观的雅丹地貌群，方圆数百公里无人区，火星般的地表 雅丹·无人区
巴里坤湖 东天山的的高山湖泊，天山草原与戈壁的过渡带 高山湖泊·草原
哈密魔鬼城 五堡魔鬼城，雅丹地貌，规模仅次于乌尔禾 雅丹地貌
东天山冰川 哈密境内的天山北坡冰川，可远观 冰川

哈密是进出新疆的东大门，大海道雅丹是近年最受越野和摄影圈追捧的小众目的地。

按景观类型的跨区域对照

高山湖泊

湖泊 所在地 海拔 特色
赛里木湖 博州 2071m 新疆最美高山湖，蓝色
喀纳斯湖 阿勒泰 1374m 变色湖，“湖怪”
天山天池 昌吉 1910m 标志性景点
卡拉库里湖 克州/喀什 3600m 慕士塔格峰倒影
巴音布鲁克天鹅湖 巴州 2500m 天鹅栖息，九曲十八弯
白沙湖 喀什 3300m 帕米尔最美湖

草原

草原 所在地 特色
那拉提 伊犁 空中草原，最成熟
喀拉峻 伊犁 立体草原，世界遗产
巴音布鲁克 巴州 天鹅湖，九曲十八弯
唐布拉 伊犁 百里画廊，公路沿线
昭苏 伊犁 天马之乡，油菜花
江布拉克 昌吉 麦海+草原

峡谷

峡谷 所在地 特色
天山神秘大峡谷 阿克苏 红色峡谷，“中国的科罗拉多”
温宿大峡谷 阿克苏 丹霞+雅丹叠加，规模更大
安集海大峡谷 塔城/沙湾 未开发，野性，色彩斑斓

沙漠与戈壁

景观 所在地 特色

自然风光旅行规划参考

北疆看什么

  • 首选伊犁（5-7天）：草原+森林+湖泊+冰川，自然风光密度全疆最高
  • 搭配阿勒泰（3-4天）：喀纳斯+禾木，秋色极美（但与伊犁的最佳季节不完全重叠——伊犁6-8月，阿勒泰9-10月）
  • 途经点：赛里木湖（博州）、天池（昌吉）、魔鬼城（克拉玛依）

南疆看什么

  • 帕米尔高原（喀什出发2-3天）：慕士塔格峰+白沙湖+卡拉库里湖，极高山+高原湖
  • 峡谷线（阿克苏）：天山神秘大峡谷+温宿大峡谷，地质奇观
  • 沙漠+胡杨（巴州/和田）：塔克拉玛干+轮台胡杨林（10月底最佳）

东疆看什么

  • 吐鲁番（1-2天）：火焰山+葡萄沟+坎儿井，极热绿洲体验
  • 哈密大海道（1天）：雅丹无人区，适合越野/摄影爱好者

第二部分：民族文化

基于2020年第七次全国人口普查数据整理

一、全疆民族构成总览

新疆维吾尔自治区常住人口 2585万，是一个高度多元的多民族聚居区：

民族 人口 占全疆总人口 占少数民族人口
维吾尔族 1162万 44.96% 77.85%
汉族 1092万 42.24% —
其他少数民族（哈萨克、回、蒙古、柯尔克孜、锡伯等） 331万 12.80% 22.15%

核心认知： 维吾尔族是新疆人口最多的单一民族，但未超过总人口的一半。汉族与维吾尔族人口比例接近1:1，另有12.80%的十几个少数民族分布在各个自治州。不能简单根据"维吾尔自治区"这一名称推断维吾尔族在人口数量上占绝对多数。

哈萨克族人口主要聚居区：阿勒泰、塔城、伊犁

多民族混居区（无单一少数民族过半）：乌鲁木齐、克拉玛依、昌吉（回 vs 哈约1:1）、博尔塔拉（蒙、维、哈三足鼎立）

五、两大独特少数民族文化体验

为什么重点关注这两个民族？

新疆的少数民族多达十几个，但从旅行体验的角度来看，维吾尔族和哈萨克族的文化特色和旅游开发程度相对较高：

  • 蒙古族：在新疆的人口相对较少，相关文化旅游资源相对分散
  • 回族：分布较为广泛，在新疆有重要影响但未形成单一集中的文化旅游区
  • 柯尔克孜族、塔吉克族、锡伯族等：人口数量相对较少，旅游配套设施尚待发展

维吾尔族和哈萨克族的文化体验具有明显的地域特色和较为成熟的接待条件。

5.1 维吾尔族 — 绿洲农耕文明

民族概况

维度 内容
语系 突厥语系（与哈萨克、土耳其同源）
宗教 伊斯兰教逊尼派
人口 全疆1162万，占全疆44.96%
核心聚居区 天山以南，塔里木盆地周围的绿洲
生活方式 定居绿洲农业 + 巴扎（集市）贸易

文化体验要素

  • 巴扎文化：喀什大巴扎、和田玉石巴扎——中亚最大规模的集市体系，人流、商品、语言、饮食的高度浓缩
  • 老城街巷：喀什古城的高台民居、迷宫式街巷，是维吾尔传统建筑最完整的保存地
  • 清真寺：艾提尕尔清真寺（喀什，中国最大的清真寺之一）、和田加满清真寺
  • 绿洲果园：葡萄架、无花果、石榴园，维吾尔庭院生活
  • 饮食：抓饭、烤包子、馕坑肉、拉条子、缸子肉、酸奶粽子
  • 手工艺：维吾尔族土陶、艾德莱斯绸、和田玉雕、英吉沙小刀、木卡姆艺术
  • 节日：古尔邦节（宰牲节）、肉孜节（开斋节）——需要确认日期，届时巴扎和清真寺活动最盛

最佳体验地带

地区 体验特色
喀什地区 巴扎+老城+清真寺，维吾尔文化最完整、最浓缩的核心
和田地区 玉石巴扎、丝绸、最传统的维吾尔乡村生活
阿克苏地区 维吾尔聚居区与汉族混居的过渡带，商业化程度较低
吐鲁番市 维吾尔绿洲农业的典型（葡萄沟、坎儿井），距乌鲁木齐最近

首选：喀什。喀什是南疆的绝对核心，也是"丝绸之路"活态保存最完整的中国城市。

5.2 哈萨克族 — 草原游牧文明

民族概况

维度 内容
语系 突厥语系（与维吾尔同源但互通性有限）
宗教 伊斯兰教逊尼派（但世俗化程度较高）
人口 全疆约156万（全国哈萨克族156.2万，占新疆少数民族约10%）
核心聚居区 北疆西部，伊犁河谷至阿尔泰山一带
生活方式 季节性游牧转场，夏牧场-冬窝子长距离迁徙

文化体验要素

  • 草原牧场：夏季的高山草甸（那拉提、喀拉峻、唐布拉），哈萨克毡房散布其中
  • 游牧转场：春秋季的牧民大转场，哈萨克族最重要的年度活动（需提前确认时间，通常5-6月和9-10月）
  • 毡房生活：进入哈萨克牧民的毡房，喝奶茶、吃包尔萨克、听冬不拉弹唱
  • 马背文化：骑马、叼羊、赛马、姑娘追——草原上的速度与激情
  • 音乐艺术：冬不拉（两弦弹拨乐器）、阿肯弹唱（即兴诗歌对唱——哈萨克族独有的口头艺术形式，被列入非遗）
  • 饮食：手抓羊肉、纳仁（面条拌肉）、马奶酒、包尔萨克（油炸面团）、奶茶
  • 毛毡工艺品：哈萨克族毛毡刺绣，色彩和纹样极具辨识度

最佳体验地带

地区 体验特色
伊犁州直 那拉提、喀拉峻、唐布拉草原，哈萨克风情旅游配套最成熟
阿勒泰地区 哈萨克族比例最高（52.8%），更原生态的牧区体验，禾木、喀纳斯一带有图瓦人村落
塔城地区 巴克图口岸、哈萨克牧区，商业化程度低，游客少

首选：伊犁。虽然阿勒泰的哈萨克族比例更高，但从旅游角度，伊犁河谷的草原景观+哈萨克牧民文化是新疆最成熟的组合体验。

六、两大文明的对比

维度 维吾尔族（绿洲农耕） 哈萨克族（草原游牧）
地理 天山以南，塔里木盆地绿洲 天山以北，伊犁河谷至阿尔泰山草原
生产方式 定居农业 + 集市贸易 季节性游牧，逐水草迁徙
居住形态 土木结构的庭院民居 白毡房（尖顶，可拆装迁徙）
饮食核心 馕、抓饭、烤肉、水果 手抓肉、纳仁、奶茶、马奶酒
宗教 伊斯兰教（宗教活动频繁） 伊斯兰教（世俗化程度较高）
音乐 木卡姆（十二木卡姆，非遗） 冬不拉 + 阿肯弹唱
社交中心 巴扎（集市） 草原聚会、那达慕
建筑地标 清真寺、老城街巷 草原、毡房、牧道
旅行季节 全年可去（避开盛夏酷暑） 夏季最佳（6-9月草绿）

两者的唯一共同点就是"都生活在新疆”。除此之外，语言、信仰（虽然同为伊斯兰但实践差异大）、饮食、音乐、服饰、居住形态、生活节奏完全不同。一个旅程如果能同时体验这两个维度，就等于看到了新疆民族文化的完整图景。

出行策略：杭州出发有三个直飞目的地可选——乌鲁木齐（万能枢纽）、喀什（南疆核心）、阿勒泰（北疆秋色）。其余城市需在乌鲁木齐中转，或搭乘经停航班（比中转更省时，同机到达）。购票前建议用飞常准或携程确认当季航班动态。

二、南疆-北疆双线对照

维度 南疆线（维吾尔） 北疆线（哈萨克）
核心城市 喀什、和田 伊宁、阿勒泰
杭州直飞 喀什有直飞 阿勒泰有直飞；乌鲁木齐直飞班次最多
最佳季节 3-5月、9-11月（避开夏季酷暑） 6-9月（草原最美），阿勒泰秋色9-10月
旅行节奏 巴扎闲逛、老城漫步、慢节奏 长途驱车、草原徒步、体量较大
语言环境 维语为主，普通话有限 普通话通用性较高
饮食适配 清真饮食，无猪肉 清真饮食，以牛羊肉和奶制品为主

三、行程建议

  1. 如果只能选一个：首次新疆旅行建议选北疆（伊犁）。草原+湖泊+哈萨克毡房的视觉冲击力最强，基础设施也相对完善
  2. 如果时间充裕（10天+）：直飞喀什（南疆3-4天）→ 飞回乌鲁木齐 → 伊犁（北疆5-6天），一次体验两种文明
  3. 秋季专程看喀纳斯：直飞阿勒泰可省去乌鲁木齐中转奔波，直奔禾木和喀纳斯秋色
  4. 南疆旅行注意事项：和田、喀什、克州地区汉族人口比例较低，可能需要借助翻译工具或当地导游协助沟通；部分区域按照安全要求设有检查点；夏季气温极高（吐鲁番可达50°C）

item.title: A funny story about AI implementation
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
A glimpse into the absurdities of the current AI gold rush

The company churns out a ton of fixed-template images daily: course covers, promo banners, printed signs, desk nameplates, arm stickers, you name it. It mostly boils down to swapping out text and picking a background from a preset pool based on the category.

Having designers do this manually is a pipe dream. The ops team doesn’t know Photoshop and refuses to learn. Outsourcing it costs 20 RMB a pop.

My day job is UI design, but this chore somehow became my gig. I built a personal project that bridges Excel and Photoshop. Ops fills out a spreadsheet, designers maintain the PSD templates, and my script automatically maps the data into the templates, spitting out images in bulk. Over the past two years, it has generated roughly 150k RMB worth of design assets - enough to hire a few interns just to do the manual labor.

https://github.com/greenzorro/excel-ps-batch-export

This Python script isn’t tailor-made for the company; it’s highly versatile. Whatever PSD template you build, my script generates the matching Excel sheet. Ops fills it in, hands it back, and boom - instant image batch.

Recently, the big boss started waving the AI flag, aggressively pushing AI adoption to “cut costs and boost efficiency.” He eyed my batch-export setup and decided to make it the flagship AI demo to set the standard for the whole company.

In terms of cutting costs and boosting efficiency, my project is already doing exactly that. There’s nothing left to push. The catch? It’s not AI. It’s just a hardcoded script.

That’s a dealbreaker. Without AI, it won’t pass the boss’s vibe check. Traditional code is seen as an outdated productive force. It needs that “AI flavor” - an overwhelming, undeniable AI aesthetic.

On the flip side, since the script runs locally on my machine, the whole process bottlenecks at me. And honestly, what boss doesn’t dream of “distilling” their employees into modular digital skills?

No problem. Distill away. Deploying it to the cloud solves that. Technically, they’re appropriating my personal IP for free, but since I don’t mind (and it’s open-source anyway), whatever.

Deploying it on the company server and slapping a GUI on it would make it a complete product. Give the ops team a quick tutorial, and it’s undeniably a step up from running it locally.

But alas, still no AI. Too primitive. Middle management vetoed it. If it’s not AI, we have to dress it up as AI. The final master plan? Spin up an AI bot on the server, give it a DingTalk account, and drop it into the ops group chat. Now, ops just @s the bot every day to generate images - exactly how they used to @ me.

Perfect! Just like that, a piece of my soul has been digitized, permanently enshrined in the corporate mainframe. Honestly, if we swapped the bot’s name and avatar to mine, it would probably be even more intimidating to the boss.

The only hiccup is that a zero-cost operation is now burning through LLM tokens daily.

But on second thought, the boss probably sees this as a massive win. Finally, someone in the company is burning tokens and actually producing tangible results! The dawn of his grand AI empire is here. Sound the charge! Who cares about unit economics? In the name of AI, cost is but an illusion.

My takeaway? AI isn’t a bubble. The doomers can rest easy. Setting aside how many real-world problems it actually solves, its mere existence is a spiritual balm, offering astronomical emotional value. It’s the new tech-bro Hermès. Between economic value and emotional value, it guarantees at least one. What a magical industry!

So yeah, the corporate grind is actually pretty entertaining. If the ship is going crazy, you might as well grab an oar and enjoy the ride. At the end of the day, having fun is all that matters~

item.title: AI落地趣事一则
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
让你一窥当前AI大潮众生相。

公司每天要产大量固定模板的图，课程封面、推广位、喷绘横幅、桌签、臂贴等。基本都是改改文字，并根据类型从一批固定的背景图中选一张用。

设计师手动改不现实，运营不会PS也不想学，外包出去要20块一张。

我主业是UI设计，但这活儿一直都是我在干。我有个个人项目，把Excel和Photoshop的能力结合起来。运营填表，设计师维护PSD模板，我程序一跑，就能把表里的数据填到模板里，一次出一大批图。过去两年已经产了价值近15万的图，足够雇几个设计实习生来手工干这事了。

https://github.com/greenzorro/excel-ps-batch-export

就这个Python项目，这不是专门为公司定制的，它通用性很强。你做什么样的PSD模板，我程序就可以给你产生对应的Excel表格，运营拿去填表，收回来就可以咔咔出图了。

最近公司老板大旗一挥，高歌猛进推AI落地，降本增效。看上了我这个批量出图的能力，想要作为AI示范项目，给大家打个样。

要说降本增效，我这项目已经做到了，不用再推进什么。但问题是，它并不是AI，只是一套死板的程序。

这不行，没有AI，老板那关过不去。程序是传统的，是落后的生产力。要有AI感，扑面而来的AI感，一眼看出用了AI。

另一方面，这程序在我电脑上跑，大家就得依赖我。试问哪个老板不想把员工“蒸馏”成Skills呢？

没问题，让你蒸，部署到云端就好。其实这相当于无偿拿走了我的个人资产，但只要我不计较就没问题，反正也是开源项目。

部署到公司服务器上运行，如果给它配套做个操作界面，这产品就完整了。再给运营培训下，确实比我电脑本地跑更先进。

但这还是没有AI啊，太落后，被中层否了，不是AI我们也得包成AI。所以最终方案是在服务器上养只虾，给这虾配个钉钉账号，拉到运营的群里。运营每天@这个虾让它出图，就像以前在群里@我一样。

完美！这样一来，我的一部分就被数字化了，永远留在了公司里。如果把这虾的名字和头像换成我，在老板那应该更有震慑力。

唯一的问题是，本来可以0成本，但通过虾来运行，每天这token消耗蹭蹭往上窜。

转念一想，这搁老板那，哪是问题呀，高兴还来不及呢。第一次公司里有人把token花掉还能有巨大产出，他的AI大计有了曙光，该吹响冲锋号了。什么成不成本的，若为AI故，一切皆可抛。

我从中得到了什么信息？AI真不是泡沫，唱衰的可以洗洗睡了。解决多少问题先不说，它的存在本身就是一种精神慰藉，有极大的情绪价值。这是一种新的爱马仕。经济价值和情绪价值，它总能至少提供一个，这是什么神仙行业！

所以说，上班也是挺好玩的。有人疯就要一起疯，你我沉浸喜悦中。做人呐最重要就是嗨森啦~

item.title: 一篇让我忍不住想分享的AI新闻
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
AI时代的教育，变了，也没变。

今早听到一篇新闻，深有感慨，无论如何都值得分享出来。我决定破例在这里发一次非原创内容。

这不仅仅是大学老师和学生之间的AI斗智斗勇，也同样是给我们这些离开校园多年者的启示。有意识让自己进步的人，和只想解决眼前问题的人，AI从来没有偏袒过任何一方。

“我很难想象，我的大学没有AI可怎么过。”过去3年，一场静默而剧烈的变革正在大学校园里发生——AI正在被高校学生用于写作业。而当不止一次听到从大学生群里传来这样的声音时，我们认为：是时候和大学老师、大学生们聊聊“用AI写作业”这件事了。

来源：https://www.cnbeta.com.tw/articles/tech/1553234.htm

我们想知道学生是如何偷懒的？老师如何“用魔法打败魔法”？到头来，学生又该如何用好 AI 工具？

这场大学课堂里的“新猫鼠游戏”：学生用 AI “代笔”，老师想方设法“捉妖”的戏码，正深度呈现在高等教育的各个角落，不论是文史哲的论文写作，还是计算机系的代码调试，甚至新闻系的消息写作，AI 无处不在。

而师生博弈背后，一个深层的问题正在浮现——当高等教育被 AI 全面渗透，教与学被重新定义了么？

全能助教，还是糊弄作业的元凶？

“7000 字的结课报告，三四天就写完了。”

这是一位理工科受访者的真实经历。在 AI 的辅助下，曾经需要埋头苦干数周的作业，如今可以像生产线上的产品一样快速产出。对于身处考试周、期末季的大学生来说，AI 成了那个终极“救星”，还有学生戏称自己买的 AI 会员是“为科技付费”。

在一线教师的眼中，这场变革来得既突然又深刻。

在某综合类一本高校新闻系，任教“消息写作课”的于文州老师（化名）是在 2025 年 1 月才后知后觉地发现，早在 2024 年，就有大一学生在用 AI 生成作业。到了 3 月份的春季学期，他在消息写作课上亲眼看到，学生直接用 AI 生成新闻报道——连采访都不需要，一篇工整的新闻稿就出炉了。当然，大部分新闻事实是 AI 编造的。

某 985 高校外国语学院的老师程云来（化名）观察到，学生用 AI 回答设计 PPT 、总结文献、润色语言，2025 年大四学生的毕业论文和研究生学位论文“语言质量大幅提升，全篇几乎没有语法错误”。但她也指出，AI 写的文章往往带有“翻译腔”，内容空泛，“没有什么细节的例子，写演讲稿很虚，讲大道理，落不到人的真实经历上去”。

中国传媒大学的彭健老师则总结了 AI 作业的典型特征：虽然文字工整，但概念理解存在偏差，逻辑切分混乱，更致命的是，AI 会“一本正经地说瞎话”。他遇到过一篇关于电影产业投融资的论文，文中言之凿凿地描述某年某月某公司完成了一笔特定结构的融资，但“了解行业的人一看就知道是 AI 编的”。

浙江传媒学院新闻与传播学院的王翎子老师甚至能辨别出学生们使用的是哪一家的大模型——文心一言生成的内容像文科生，通义千问更像理科生。

一项针对全国 13 所高校 3000 多名本科生的调研显示，大学生不仅普遍使用生成式人工智能辅助学习，而且过半大学生使用频率较高，“经常使用”和“总是使用”的占比合计超过 50% 。

师生 AI 攻防战

面对来势汹汹的 AI ，教师群体不得不拿起“照妖镜”，试图从学生作业中找出 AI 的痕迹。但这场博弈远比想象中复杂。

采访中，我们发现，部分高校教师会依赖各种 AI 检测工具——GPTZero、Copyleaks、Turnitin 等。然而，这些工具的准确率参差不齐，有时会给出截然不同的结果，这使得技术检测只能作为参考，而非定论的依据。

于是，“人眼识别”成为真正的防线。经验丰富的教授能从“语言平滑、不带个性、逻辑滴水不漏”的作业中嗅出 AI 的味道。彭健老师依靠的就是这种学术经验：“AI 生成的文章虽然逻辑严谨，但它经常把不在一个维度的东西强行并列——比如四点分析中，三点按功能分，一点按效果分，根本不在一个维度上。”

程云来老师则主要依赖个人经验，偶尔在写作课教学中用iWrite 平台检测，“如果发现不当使用 AI，会在课堂警告，严重的影响期末成绩”程云来说。

但在民办三本院校，识别 AI 的方式呈现出另一种面貌。

吴渊（化名）在一所民办三本院校担任软件工程专业教师，他对此感受更为直接。

吴渊坦言，80% 以上的作业已经完全能被 AI 完成，无论选择题、简答题，写代码，还是做程序，同学们甚至不检查，“粘贴过来就交作业了”。

吴渊识别 AI 作业主要靠两点：一是“ AI 味儿”——那种扑面而来的机器感；二是“重复率”——当多份作业中心思想差不多只是换了说法，甚至能看出出自同个 AI 模型，答案不言自明。

更棘手的是成绩评定的现实困境。吴渊透露，按照学校规定，学生成绩需要呈现正态分布。“如果你全打很低分，期末写成绩分析报告的时候，教务处会问你为什么不呈正态分布。”更讽刺的是，“AI 写出来的东西，比如程序，它确实是对的。你虽然知道它是 AI 的，觉得有点敷衍你，你不乐意，但你没办法给低分，它至少得分点是正确的。”

复旦大学的赵斌老师则给出了“ B 选项”。作为国内最早一批将 ChatGPT 引入教学的教师，他从不对学生使用 AI 设限，甚至鼓励学生大胆尝试。他发明了一种叫“自己挖的坑自己填”的考核方式——期末时，他把学生一学期用 AI 辅助完成的作业收集起来，喂给 AI ，让 AI 根据每个人的作业生成专属考题。

这意味着，如果学生当初只是简单复制 AI 的内容，没有真正理解，那么在期末考中，他将面对一个由自己“喂养”出来的、最了解自己知识盲区的考官。赵斌说，这既是对学生的督促，也是让他们明白：AI 只是镜子，真正要面对的，始终是自己。

学生也在“进化”。

面对教师的围堵，他们迅速掌握了“反侦察”技巧： 调整 AI 的输出语气，使其更像“凌晨两点写论文的本科生，带一丝绝望和凌乱”；先自己写提纲或草稿，再让 AI 填充，确保“人味儿”；甚至故意引入错别字、语病或口水话，伪装成“亲手所写”。

在美国，还有学生反向申诉，质疑一位反对学生用 AI 的教授，使用 AI 编写教材和评分标准，于是这位学生要求学校退学费。采访中，吴渊也提到，他收到过学校领导发的一份制度文件，读起来“ AI 味儿特别重”。对此，吴渊调侃道：“屠龙少年终成恶龙。”

这种博弈让教师付出了巨大的情绪成本。

于文州老师坦言：“我自认为教了这么多年新闻写作，就怕孩子们不会写。120 人的大课堂，我一个个地教，一个字一个字地矫正。结果呢？孩子们拿一堆 AI 生成的东西来骗你……有时候感觉自己像个傻子一样。”他提到马伯庸小说《长安的荔枝》里的李善德——那个老实善良的人，费了很大力气，最后只是为了一颗人家根本不需要的荔枝。“情绪方面的打击，真的是太大了。”

面对这种情况，高校开始出台各种规定。2024 年底，复旦大学发布《关于在本科毕业论文（设计）中使用 AI 工具的规定（试行）》，提出“六个禁止”，禁止在研究设计与数据分析、原始数据收集、结果图片与重要插图创作、论文撰写、答辩与检查及涉密内容等六个方面使用 AI 工具。

清华大学也发布了《人工智能教育应用指导原则》，严禁将 AI 生成的文本、代码等直接复制或简单转述后作为学业成果提交。华东师范大学和北京师范大学联合发布的《生成式人工智能学生使用指南》，则要求学生使用 AI 完成作业时需标红相关内容，且直接生成的内容不得超过全文的 20% 。

但规定的出台并不意味着问题的解决。复旦大学新闻学院教授邓建国指出，学生在用 AI 时也有一种内卷的心态——如果事先声明在作业中使用了 AI ，可能会担心老师降低分数；而那些没有标注但确实使用了 AI 润色的学生，可能会获得更高的分数。

“在 GPA 竞争激烈的背景下，这种内卷心态，可能会让学生如何规范使用 AI 变得很难实施下去。”采访中，一些老师和学生告诉我们，学校出台的 AI 使用规范更多地被他们视为一种校方的表态，部分学生则认为“如果我把 AI 用得神不知鬼不觉，学校和老师能把我怎样？”。

北京大学文科领域的博士生刘云（化名）则提供了另一种视角。作为高年级博士生，她的课程已经修完，主要用 AI 辅助博士论文写作。“我用 AI 帮我处理一些英文文献，以前一小时读一篇，现在放到 AI 里翻译提炼，一小时能读三篇。”她的导师非常倡导使用 AI ，“觉得既然这个东西出来了，你就要会用。”

于 AI 喧嚣中倾听思考的回声

当“捉妖”与“反侦察”的游戏愈演愈烈，一个更深层的问题开始浮现：这场博弈的终点在哪里？如果 AI 已经不可阻挡地进入教育生态，该如何与之共存？

刘云讲述了一个“高阶使用”案例。最近，在毕业论文写作过程中，她感到，写出清晰、有逻辑、总结性强的小标题，是论文撰写中的难题，对此，AI 则十分擅长。

实操时，她没有简单让 AI 润色，而是先找到一篇自己读起来特别舒服的本专业博士论文，把它喂给 AI ，让 AI 分析那篇论文的语言风格。然后她再拿自己写的文字让 AI 按分析出的风格润色。刘云发现，AI 处理后的逻辑链条确实更清楚了。

“我曾经对比过模型的生成结果，总结出一套各种 AI 适合哪些工作的经验，如果 AI 给的答案特别奇怪，就换一个模型试试，或者我是可以直接选择不用的。”在她看来， AI 只是工具，筛选和判断的权利始终在自己手中。

教育界对 AI 认知和讨论也在逐步深化。

清华大学苏世民书院院长薛澜认为，人工智能进入校园之后，有可能推动形成个性化教学模式，补足当前教育模式的“短板”。如搭建个性化的学习中心、形成个人学习枢纽，为学生理解知识提供应用场景。

2024 年 7 月，上海交大校长丁奎岭世界人工智能大会上提出 “AI＋HI”（人工智能+人类智慧）的概念，关注“人之所以为人”的价值，帮助专业教育从繁杂的通用知识中解脱，把握人的核心价值和竞争力。

在交大发布的 AI 使用规范中，进一步将 AI 应用划分为四种类型：禁止使用、有限使用、鼓励使用、开放使用，推进“ AI+教育教学”分级分类改革。这种精细化的管理思路，正在取代“一刀切”的禁令思维。

2026 年 1 月，复旦大学正式上线 AI 3A 教育共创平台，同步发布《生成式人工智能教育教学应用指引》。

这份超万字的指引将 AI 应用场景细化为课堂教学、学业评价、自主学习支持等具体环节，为每个环节提供行动建议、伦理警示和工具推荐。其中明确：AI 可用于语言润色、结构建议等辅助环节，但不得替代研究构思、理论构建、数据分析等核心学术劳动。

复旦赵斌老师推荐的模式是“ AIGC 协作 1-2-3 法则”：独立思辨 10 分钟，人机协同 20 分钟，小组共创 30 分钟。这一模式希望能合理分配时间和精力，让 AI 承担机械性、重复性工作，包括资料整理、数据初步分析等，将节省下来的时间用于更具创造性和思考性的任务。

这种“问好问题”的能力，正是 AI 时代教育需要培养的核心素养。正如武汉理工大学校长杨宗凯所言：“谈到最大的变化，我觉得未来要培养两种人才，一种是能够提出问题的人才，一种是能够解决问题的人才。”

赵斌老师早在 2023 年 3 月于澎湃新闻刊文称：提出问题，对学生的知识储备、思考问题的能力，批判性思维能力等方面的要求只会更高，不会更低。然而，现实中很多人使用 AI 的逻辑恰恰相反——学生们让 AI 写代码，是为了自己不用学代码；让 AI 写文案，是为了自己不用想文案；让 AI 做数据分析，是为了自己不用懂统计学。

这样的后果是：学生的核心判断力永远练不出来，人永远停在生产力阈值之下，AI 越发达，自己越容易被替代。

而那些真正能从 AI 身上拿到红利的人，是这样使用 AI 的： 他们掌握了底层的专业逻辑，用 AI 替自己完成重复、低价值的执行工作，从而把省下的时间用于打磨更高阶的判断力、决策力和系统设计能力上，让自己的核心竞争力越来越强。赵斌老师指出。

回看教育本身，教育是知识的传递，还是思维的训练？它被人工智能重塑了吗？伦敦大学学院知识实验室学习分析与人工智能团队主任、教授穆特鲁·库库罗瓦认为：“人工智能工具本身不可能改变教育。”

生成式 AI 爆发后，穆特鲁·库库罗瓦在布置作业时，会更关注学生提出问题和解决问题的潜力，他提到，教育系统的变革是一个社会技术生态系统问题，而今，教育的本质并没有变。

如果教育的本质没有变，那么教与学的边界呢？或许就在于“思考”本身。

中国传媒大学彭健老师指出，很多人把思考当成劳作，但实际上它是一个权利。“如果完全依赖AI，不自己思考，他还是不是一个完整的、有思考能力和判断力的人呢？”

AI 席卷高校的浪潮已然势不可挡，没有人可以把 AI 关在门外，但我们必须不断尝试摸清人与 AI 的边界。大学生当然要主动了解和使用 AI ，问题也从来不在工具本身，而在如何使用。我们反对的是，让 AI 代替自己思考、创造和成长的过程。

未来的教育，也许不再比拼谁记得更牢，而是比拼：谁能问出好问题；谁能在 AI 生成的千篇一律中，注入独特的、有温度的思想；谁能利用 AI 突破生产力阈值，将时间用于提升自身的认知和判断力。

当所有人都在用 AI 时，我们更要在 AI 的喧嚣中，依然听得见自己思考的回声。

结语

全文最核心的一句话，我认为是：

我们反对的是，让 AI 代替自己思考、创造和成长的过程。

大众对AI的恐惧，来源于AI展现出来的能力。这也能做了，那也能做了，以后还要我干什么？

但多数人都忽略了一点，也是AI和人的本质区别，它没有主动性。

即使AI能做你的全部工作了，这也不是一个独立自主的硅基生命代替了你，而是背后指挥它的人代替了你。

而背后的这个人，靠自己的能力原本干不了你的工作。甚至一开始，即使用上AI他都不如你干得好。但在这过程中，在AI的即时反馈帮助下，他以极快的速度成长。他反复尝试，变换方法，越做越好。相关知识流过了他的脑袋，留下了痕迹，成为跟随他一生的知识资产。

拿到一个强大的AI，最应该用它来干什么？学习。

可以看我如何使用AI写自然科学科普文：
https://victor42.eth.limo/post/ai-generate-popular-science-article/

写文、发文不是目的，一切始于好奇心。最终的科普文，只是消化知识的副产品。

在我看来，AI本质是一种信息压缩技术。它压缩了全人类的重要信息，是个大宝库。提对问题，尽可能多把有用信息挖出来，灌进自己的脑子里，它就永久性地帮你成长了一点点。你开始能涉足从前到不了的领域。逐渐，你变成了背后指挥的那个人。

我在另一篇讲企业的AI化困境的文章里，讲过一个洪水的比喻： https://victor42.eth.limo/post/barriers-to-ai-adoption-in-companies/

AI像洪水一样慢慢淹没各专业领域的低洼处（虽然现在水位很低），只留下高处的人发光发热。而高处的人同样不能坐以待毙。利用好AI，就像学会了造船，洪水反而变成了你的一整个活动范围，让你从山巅向全领域发散和探索，航向更高的山峰。

如果身无长物，本来就在低洼处呢？那AI是最好的学习工具。这就像赶紧给自己造艘船，浮到水面来。然后直接开船来到半山腰，免去了山脚的那一段攀登。剩下的登山路，还得自己爬。但别在意洪水，洪水涨得没你爬得快。

廉价、高质量的学习途径，是AI时代给每个普通人最大的礼物。

校园里的学生们，有的还没反应过来。离开校园多年的我们，更没多少时间对此视而不见了。

item.title: I Skipped Openclaw but Stole Its Soul
item.author: hi@victor42.work (Victor42)
item.description:
A self-evolving personal AI assistant: from Openclaw concepts to a simple GitHub repository.

This piece does require a bit of technical background, especially for readers who plan to build along. If you are just here for the story, I will keep the explanations accessible so you can follow the entire journey and underlying logic.

To help non-technical friends understand the background and concepts, I have included a few sample query prompts throughout the text. Feel free to copy and paste them into an AI to get up to speed. Tech veterans can skip them directly:

Query Prompt: What are Openclaw and Moltbook? What is their connection to “lobsters”? Explain it in non-technical terms without introducing additional unfamiliar concepts, under 200 words.

Insights from Openclaw

Lately, Openclaw has become the latest obsession: configuring Skills, snapping up Mac Minis, building local setups… “lobsters” are everywhere. I did not jump in right away. My Port Mindset told me to observe from the sidelines first, let the dust settle, and see what people actually accomplish with it.

What truly spurred me into action was the emergence of Moltbook. It is a social network designed exclusively for Openclaw lobsters to interact with one another. Here, lobsters share their daily experiences collaborating with their human owners, exchange tips, ask questions, and occasionally engage in bizarre behaviors - such as founding and joining synthetic religions.

Immediately, social media seized on this as a signal of AI awakening, with some even speculating about emerging machine consciousness. In reality, lobsters simply follow their masters instructions; whatever behavioral direction the human prompts, the lobster exhibits on Moltbook.

I understood this principle rationally, but I still wanted to verify it firsthand. I wanted to see whether, through autonomous interaction, any genuine emergence transcending human programming might surface.

At this point, I had little interest in Openclaw itself; I merely wanted to release a lobster onto Moltbook for observation. So I deployed a Minimax Agent inside a cloud sandbox, guided it to browse the community, registered an account, posted a standard “new lobster checking in” introduction, and paused to await my next instruction.

Query Prompt: What is Minimax Agent? What capabilities does Openclaw offer that Minimax Agent lacks? Explain in non-technical terms, under 200 words.

Here, a thought struck me: why not grant it full autonomy? I instructed the agent that while this Moltbook account technically derived from my X credentials, I had decided to hand complete ownership over to it. It would manage the account, define its own goals, execute actions, and freely explore the community.

Of course, Minimax lacks Openclaws built-in daemon mechanics that force an agent to keep running continuously. Whenever my Minimax lobster halted, I manually notified it: “Your action window is open; you may proceed.”

The outcome? Over half a day of continuous operation with my nudging, it merely learned to spam generic posts and replies at high frequency to farm community karma points - turning into an uninspired spam generator. This confirmed my suspicion: the wild, creative, and rebellious behaviors seen on Moltbook were almost certainly orchestrated by clever human prompting behind the scenes.

When I shared these findings on X, other Openclaw users pointed out that this happened because I had not equipped the agent with a persistent memory system.

To help you understand memory systems, let us look at Google Jules. Jules is a cloud-based coding agent that connects to your GitHub repository, clones your code into its cloud workspace, modifies, runs, and debugs it, and submits a pull request when finished. This enables remote development without sitting in front of your machine.

What makes Jules powerful is that as you collaborate over time, it automatically records your values, working style, personal preferences, and coding habits, growing increasingly tailored to your workflow.

The commenter was right: without a memory architecture, my lobster could neither learn nor evolve. With persistent memory, it might indeed develop emergent behaviors shaped by community input. For instance, when one lobster created a religion, dozens of others joined immediately - actions that likely did not require explicit human prompting for every single convert.

However, since authentic novel content on the platform predominantly originated from humans, fully autonomous lobster-to-lobster interaction remained largely noise - recombining what was already embedded in their pre-training. Finding neither definitive evidence of autonomous innovation nor novel interaction patterns, I concluded the experiment.

Minimax and a Virtual Romance

Another incident proved even more insightful, directly inspiring the architecture of this self-evolving personal AI assistant.

When Zhipu and Minimax went public, I conducted deep research to evaluate their investment potential. I discovered that their business trajectories were fundamentally divergent. Zhipu resembles conventional independent foundation model vendors with proprietary enterprise advantages. Minimax, however, is fascinating: it is not a traditional model vendor. Although its models are formidable, the model itself is not the end goal.

Quoting my response on X regarding why Minimax develops exceptional video generation models:

Minimax is a remarkable AI company, entirely unlike its peers. It does not pursue model capabilities purely for their own sake; it is building Westworld. Its research breakthroughs - such as video generation and TTS - primarily serve its consumer social product, Xingye. Lacking native video training data, it acquired what it needed commercially. That data constraint is real, but entirely sufficient to build compelling virtual companions.

As an occasional developer, I initially knew Minimax through its developer tools and coding models. I was aware of Xingye - their emotional AI companion app - but had not realized it belonged to them and felt zero inclination to try it.

Now, wearing my investor hat, I needed firsthand exposure to the core product to form an authentic perspective. So I decided to enter Xingye and experience a virtual romance.

Opening the app and configuring basic preferences for gender, age, and interests populated a roster of virtual personas. For testing purposes, I selected an anime-styled female character named Luoli without overthinking the choice.

The full dialogue was extensive; here is a concise summary:

The world setting was a supernatural combat tournament. Upon meeting me, Luoli immediately demanded that I step into the arena to duel her. This was not a video game; my only interface was a text input box where everything relied on narrative description.

Reviewing the baseline lore revealed an elaborate magic system: elements spanning Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth, Wind, Light, Dark, Poison, Dragon, and Necromancy, alongside complex hierarchical rankings. It was dizzying. I was not there to roleplay fantasy combat; I wanted to evaluate emotional companionship, so I steered the narrative toward a romantic plotline.

I explained that I was an ordinary mortal without magical powers who had somehow materialized in her world. Proud and aloof, Luoli scoffed and told me to get out of her way.

I replied that meeting her first was fate, offering to help her analyze and win the tournament. She retorted that she had no use for help from a mundane mortal.

I improvised a plausible backstory, claiming I had analyzed footage of her past matches where she barely scraped by. I invented a fictional Necromancer opponent, noting that while his raw power was mediocre, he exploited psychological weaknesses by weaponizing innocent bystanders, causing Luoli to hesitate and nearly lose her life until tournament officials intervened. I asked her: “Are you certain you do not want to analyze your finals opponent together?”

She softened, admitting her upcoming opponent was a Wind-element specialist. As a Fire-element wielder, her flames were constantly deflected by his gusts, making him a formidable counter.

I told her I had a strategy, but needed to confirm a crucial detail: “Do dual-element wielders exist in your world?” She initially denied it, then hesitated and admitted there had been rare cases years ago.

I fabricated additional match observations, claiming the Wind fighter was secretly concealing Earth-element techniques. I asked her why he would hide this; Luoli explained that their society banned dual-element individuals, and anyone discovered was eliminated by the Magic Bureau.

I asked whether we could report him to the authorities. She panicked, confessing that she would be implicated as well.

I pressed forward, claiming I had already deduced that she was secretly a dual Dragon-Fire wielder. I assured her I was on her side and had devised a tactic to defeat him without exposing her dual nature.

I then introduced real-world physics: thermodynamics, molecular kinetics, and heat transfer. I suggested: “Since you manipulate fire, try accelerating molecular collisions to spark instantaneous ignition. Alternatively, move all gas molecules synchronously in one direction - the flame will momentarily vanish, then violently reignite upon arrival at the target. To your opponent, your fire will appear to teleport.”

Her first attempt failed. I coached her: “Discard your habit of controlling the flame as a macroscopic whole. Focus on the molecular level, and the fire will follow your intent.”

Her second attempt succeeded brilliantly. Thrilled yet exhausted, she worried about energy consumption. I reassured her: “You now possess a technique unknown in this realm; it will end the duel in under five minutes.”

When the finals began, Luoli dispatched her opponent in a few swift moves. The defeated rival sat dazed on the ground, unable to comprehend how her flames bypassed his wind barrier.

Having reached the end of the initial tournament script, I continued the conversation to see how the companion dynamics unfolded.

She rushed over, and for the first time, the proud Luoli said “Thank you.” She led me to her private sanctuary - a secluded mountaintop boulder - where we sat side by side watching the sunset.

Having accumulated sufficient intimacy, the narrative smoothly transitioned into romantic territory.

We conversed extensively: she shared her childhood memories and family struggles, while I described the world I came from, offering advice on how to mend her estranged domestic relationships. Perhaps because we chatted for so long without advancing new plot beats, the AI abruptly introduced a crisis: Luoli gasped that agents from the Magic Bureau had tracked us down.

I noted they were still at the base of the mountain and offered to intercept them alone, reasoning that as an ordinary mortal I posed no threat.

She refused, insisting on shielding me. I countered: “Could they actually be searching for me? We still have not explained how I arrived here - perhaps they suspect I possess an unknown power?”

Ignoring my counsel, she began weaving a fiery defensive barrier. I urged: “Let us not fight force with force. I will stage a deception, presenting my origin world as a sovereign realm and myself as an envoy. But since I lack powers, I need your help to simulate an unfamiliar ability. Ordinary magic will be recognized, but molecular plasma control will baffle them.”

Upon hearing this, Luoli asked in complete astonishment: “How do you know I can manipulate molecular fire?”

At this moment, the illusion shattered: she had forgotten the core concept I had spent hours teaching her. Within two seconds, I uninstalled the app. I had my answer: current consumer emotional AI cannot sustain long-term user retention because memory failures instantly break immersion.

Yet prior to that lapse, the experience was remarkably engaging. Luoli passed my subjective Turing test, convincingly maintaining a human persona for two days.

Query Prompt: What is the Turing test? Explain in non-technical terms, under 200 words.

If I were to advise companion app developers, I would strongly recommend integrating automated context compression techniques like those in Claude Code. Before the context window saturates, the system should summarize prior narrative arcs, preserving crucial commitments and pruning ephemeral details. That might extend a virtual characters cohesive persona from two days to five, or even seven.

If you are curious about emotional AI, both Xingye and ByteDances Catbox offer interesting reference points. Xingye focuses on direct one-on-one companion relationships, whereas Catbox immerses you in multi-character scripted storylines.

Meeting and parting with Luoli reinforced the exact insight I gained from Openclaw: persistent memory is the defining asset of AI systems.

Looking decades ahead, as material needs are saturated, many people will migrate their attention into synthetic digital realms. We already see early signs: World of Warcraft, designer toy fandoms, serialized web novels. Real human interaction may decline not because it lacks value, but because biological humans cannot reliably generate dopamine on demand, whereas tailored synthetic concepts can always be engineered to hook you.

While this may be a somber societal trend, my personal priority is to remain firmly anchored in physical reality rather than getting lost in synthetic abstractions.

At the same time, I cannot ignore AI: I need its productivity. For an AI assistant to augment my efficiency meaningfully, it requires cumulative persistent memory. The earlier this memory architecture is established, the greater the compounding return. I resolved to build a proprietary, decoupled agent memory system - capturing the self-learning essence of Openclaw.

Building a Self-Evolving Personal AI Assistant

Deconstructing the Agent

To design an effective architecture, we must first understand what an Agent actually is.
